note: Tool-mapped workflow recipes for houdini-bridge-mcp — GUIDES, not gospel. Each recipe is ONE proven way to do X with this server's real typed tools; Houdini offers many valid approaches, so treat a recipe as a worked example to understand and ADAPT, not the only path or an authoritative spec. Each is an ordered sequence of tools plus the parameters that actually move the result, with a per-step landmark (the OUT_ null to plant) + verify (the cheap read to run). Data-only: recipes never run themselves. Heavy solves/renders/caches are WIRE-ONLY by design — the recipe builds the network; you fire the cook. Distilled from SideFX docs + community TD references; validate exact param values against the live node UI for hero work.

steps.note: builds the vellum solver from the input mesh as CLOTH. Input = the cloth geo (a subdivided grid/garment).

key_params.constraint_type: cloth (stretch+bend); softbody / grain are the siblings
key_params.thickness: collision thickness (~ mesh edge length; too small = tunneling)

steps.note: add pins/attaches so the cloth hangs (e.g. pin a point group to target). Wire after the cloth, before the solver where possible.

wrangle_opportunity.why: custom pin/stiffness mask: write per-point f@stiffness or a pin group from a painted mask / bbox test so the flag holds at the pole and softens at the fly edge - graded constraint weighting the uniform constraint node cannot author.

steps.note: register a collider (a ground/prop) so the cloth drapes over it.
WIRE-ONLY: File Cache 2.0, confined path. You fire the multi-frame cook.

Grains/sand: constraint_type=grain on a point cloud.
Pre-drape a garment onto a character with vellum_drape before the shot.

Cloth passes through the collider -> raise thickness or substeps.
Pin a group with vellum_constraint (pin) — don't freeze the whole mesh.

recipes.title: Procedural terrain: build -> noise -> erode -> mask -> export
recipes.summary: Heightfield terrain from scratch (or an imported DEM), eroded and masked, converted to mesh and written.

steps.note: start a heightfield and displace it with noise (or begin from import_heightfield on a real DEM).
hydraulic/thermal erosion — the step that makes terrain read as REAL (channels, talus). The expensive cook.
build a mask from slope/height/occlusion (e.g. steep = rock, flat = grass) for later layering/scatter.

wrangle_opportunity.why: custom terrain mask math: combine slope, height band and curvature into one f@mask layer (e.g. snow only above H and below slope S) - a compound rule the single-feature mask nodes cannot express in one pass.
wrangle_opportunity.consent: run via set_attrib_expr ONLY if the user has enabled allow_attrib_expr (explicit consent); otherwise propose the VEX text via vex_reference for the user to paste by hand, and EXPLAIN what it does and why (this is a teaching moment, not just an action).

steps.note: composite layers (rock/soil/snow) driven by the mask.
convert the heightfield volume to a polygon mesh for texturing/export.

key_params.resolution: polys follow the heightfield voxel count — watch the budget

steps.note: WIRE-ONLY: write the mesh to a confined .bgeo/.obj (or export_pointcloud for a cloud). You fire the write.

rop_opportunity.why: the eroded, masked heightfield is ready to write; exporting the raw heightfield layers/tiles (height + masks) for an engine or DEM is a gated file WRITE distinct from the poly geo export.
rop_opportunity.propose_via: heightfield_output builds + wires the heightfield export ROP (per-layer/tiled); the human fires the write.

Vegetation: scatter with density_attrib driven by the heightfield mask (scatter/biome_scatter).
Texture the mesh with assign_usd_material projection=triplanar (no UVs needed).
tips: Erosion is the cost hotspot — probe `mem` and keep iterations modest at high res.
convert_heightfield polycount = voxel count; downres the heightfield or polyreduce after.
Masks are the currency: erode -> maskbyfeature -> layer/scatter all chain off them.

recipes.summary: Procedural hard-surface modeling from curves/primitives: sweep or revolve a profile, boolean parts, then bevel/extrude detail and clean.

steps.note: lay down the backbone/spine or a cross-section profile (or start from create_primitive for a base solid).
sweep a cross-section along the backbone -> a surface (pipes, rails, mouldings). Or use revolve for a lathe form, skin to loft between profiles.

key_params.cross_section: input curve or a built-in tube/square/ribbon

steps.note: combine/subtract parts (cut panels, add bosses). The core hard-surface op.
bevel the hard edges so they catch light (no CG edge is perfectly sharp).

wrangle_opportunity.why: curvature-weighted bevel: measure convexity and write a per-point/edge bevel weight so only sharp convex edges round off - an attribute-driven bevel profile the uniform bevel node cannot express.
wrangle_opportunity.consent: run via set_attrib_expr ONLY if the user has enabled allow_attrib_expr (explicit consent); otherwise propose the VEX text via vex_reference for the user to paste by hand, and EXPLAIN what it does and why (this is a teaching moment, not just an action).

steps.note: extrude panels/greebles; distance_attrib drives per-face depth for variation.
fuse coincident points / fix normals before export or subdivision.

variants: Lathe form: revolve a profile instead of sweep.
Loft: skin across several stacked cross-section curves.
Mirror the half you modelled with mirror (weld on the seam).
Array parts with copy_to_points (id_attrib for a variant/piece match).
tips: Bevel AFTER boolean, not before — booleans hate pre-beveled edges.
Keep quads where you can (facet/divide only where needed) for clean subdivision.
Clean/fuse before subdivide or the mesh cracks at boolean seams.

recipes.title: Fix packed-piece orient/pivot after an RBD sim (intrinsic rebuild)
recipes.summary: After a packed RBD sim, rebuild each piece’s orient/pivot from its packed intrinsics so downstream copy/transform reads them correctly — done with ONE safe-VEX wrangle, no bespoke node.

steps.note: run a point wrangle over the packed pieces reading the packed transform intrinsics into p@orient / v@pivot. primintrinsic() is allowlisted in safe-VEX.

key_params.snippet: matrix3 m = primintrinsic(0, "packedfulltransform", @ptnum); p@orient = quaternion(m); v@pivot = primintrinsic(0, "pivot", @ptnum);

variants: Read "packedlocaltransform" instead for local-space orient.
tips: This is a data-only VEX read (no writers) — it goes through the same validated set_attrib_expr lane.
If orient looks wrong downstream, confirm the copy/transform is actually reading p@orient + v@pivot.
recipes.classify: fix packed-piece orient/pivot after an RBD sim (intrinsic rebuild via one safe-VEX read)
recipes.governance: data-only VEX read (no writers) through the validated set_attrib_expr lane: primintrinsic() is allowlisted. Run over POINTS on packed pieces - packedfulltransform gives world orient, packedlocaltransform gives local-space orient.

recipes.title: Large-scale stormy ocean: big-waves spectrum grid + low-res FLIP + point-deform distortion
recipes.summary: The divide-and-combine ocean shot: a NON-simulated big-waves ocean grid, a low-res FLIP sim of only the foreground/boat area, then distort the sim BY the big waves with point-deform. Animate the boat on the result; up-res later for splashes. (Grounded in SideFX masterclass "Water FX | Stormy Seas" pt.1.)

steps.note: BIG WAVES (not simulated): the full Ocean Spectrum + Evaluate grid driving the underlying rolling swell — spectrum_type/depth/swell/fetch/wind give the deep 'stormy' look ocean_surface can't reach. Returns a reusable spectrum SOP so the SAME deterministic waves can also feed ocean_source coupling.

key_params.fetch: km the wind blows — BIGGER fetch = bigger, farther-apart waves
key_params.depth: shallower steepens the swell; deep (~3000) = open-ocean rollers

steps.note: LOW-RES FLIP over ONLY the foreground/boat area (not the whole ocean). Driven by a SEPARATE local-wind spectrum. Small container = fast.

key_params.particlesep: 0.1 low-res starter (~0.06 here); do not go too low or the up-res look shifts
key_params.size: shrink to the boat area only (~25-28), not the full spectrum extent

steps.note: add DRAG/resistance to the particles (masterclass uses a POP Drag ~0.01) so the water is not too energetic. (pop_drag = pop_force ftype=drag; flip_force/pop_force cover the general case.)

verify.cheap: (wire-only - POP drag force on the solver)

steps.note: mesh the particles (surface polygons). Trim the boundaries (disable closed boundaries) so the sim edge is not a wall.

THE KEY STEP: distort the low-res FLIP surface BY the big-waves grid. mesh=sim surface, rest=FLAT grid, deformed=big-waves grid. Rest and deformed MUST share point/prim count. Raise point-radius min (~10) for clean deformation.
animate the boat on the distorted surface with SEPARATE transforms per axis (tx flat / ty / rotation) — easier to tweak than one node. Center the pivot ( centroid).
keyframe a SLOW boat move (against the storm ~12m over ~200 frames); start after ~frame 48 (ocean still settling before that).

variants: Open/distant shot: cheat — do NOT simulate; drive more with the spectrum grid + tricks.
Close-up: build a SEPARATE high-res confined sim for just that area (do not reuse the wide one).
Up-res: run a higher-res sim WITH the animated boat for splashes/interaction after the low-res look is locked.
tips: DIVIDE the shot into many small combined sims (big waves / small waves / boat splash) — never one huge sim that must do everything; each is a base for the next and stays fixable.

ocean_spectrum LANDED (this gap is closed): full Ocean Spectrum authoring (spectrum_type/depth/gravity/seed/swell/fetch/wind_dir/dir_bias/loop) + Evaluate onto a grid, returning the reusable spectrum SOP. ocean_surface remains the quick 6-param version.
Real deep-ocean waves ROLL (mountains), they do not barrel like shallow-reef waves — emphasise rolling swell + wind chop breaking into whitewater.

Provenance (frame-verify money moments): spectrum params ~26:00-38:00; low-res FLIP + POP drag ~41:00-51:00; particle fluid surface ~52:00-55:00; POINT DEFORM ~55:00-59:00; boat anim ~60:00-73:00. FRAME-VERIFIED ~56:40: the point-deform stage pulls the big-waves geo into the wavetank net via an Object Merge ('BigWaves' -> /obj/BigWaves_geo/OUT_*, Transform='Into Specified Object') — the cross-network object_merge idiom (= bridge_into xformtype=1).
recipes.classify: large-scale ocean shot / stormy seascape - non-simulated big-waves spectrum + low-res FLIP, combined by point-deform
recipes.governance: pointdeform's rest (FLAT grid) and deformed (big-waves grid) MUST share identical point/prim count or the distortion is garbage; keep the FLIP sim tiny (boat area only, narrowband=true) - never simulate the whole ocean.

recipes.title: High-res boat FLIP: inverse-deformed collider + custom-pscale mesh + edge-matched patches
recipes.summary: The production high-res half of the stormy-seas shot: prep an animated boat as a VDB collider, INVERSE-point-deform it so it collides correctly against the FLAT sim tank, run a droplet-aware high-res FLIP, then mesh from scratch with a vorticity/velocity-driven p-scale, and flatten + re-distort the patch edges so this sim tiles seamlessly with neighbouring ocean patches. (Grounded in SideFX masterclass 'Water FX | Stormy Seas' pt.2.)

steps.note: COLLIDER PREP: trail on the animated boat to compute velocity from the CENTRAL (before+after frame) difference — the sim needs v on the collider. Recompute the trail AGAIN after any later deformation (velocities change).
keep only the parts that actually touch water (hull/deck/cockpit/keel/rudder/propeller) via named groups; drop the mast/sails for the MAIN flip (add back only if splashes need them).
cap open holes -> watertight geometry before VDB (masterclass uses a poly-cap). polyfill/mesh_repair cover this.

convert the watertight boat to an SDF VDB. Resolution ~0.08 keeps thin parts; too coarse loses detail. Then dilate/erode slightly to close pinholes (VDB reshape — the vdb_reshape tool). Cache the collision VDB (boat_collision_vdb).

THE INVERSE DEFORM (key insight): the sim runs on the FLAT tank, but the boat is animated to sit on the DISTORTED big-ocean. So invert the Part-1 point-deform: rest = the DISTORTED big-waves grid, deformed = the FLAT grid. The boat looks twisted in isolation but collides correctly against the flat sim; it un-distorts back to the right place at render. Raise the min point-radius for a clean deform; recompute trail after.

HIGH-RES sim: WIDER container than the low-res (splashes must break + propagate, and neighbour patches attach), same spectrum as low-res. particlesep ~0.03-0.04 (0.03 amazing, 0.05-0.06 if machine-limited). Top (+Y) open = kill; other walls closed.

key_params.size: wider than low-res for splash headroom

steps.note: DROPLETS: group particles whose 'droplet' density attribute > ~0.1 (particles that flew off the main fluid) into 'droplet_group' so forces can treat them differently. Enable Droplets in the FLIP solver (raise threshold), enable ID + vorticity attributes (save-as-default).

WIND on droplets ONLY: a POP Wind restricted to droplet_group so airborne particles catch the wind but submerged ones don't. velocity ~(6,0,3) aligned ~45deg to the waves; SWIRL SIZE ~3 so neighbouring particles move coherently (gusts), not per-particle noise. (pop_wind = pop_force ftype=wind, pop_drag = pop_force ftype=drag.)

boat as a STATIC OBJECT with the collide relationship INVERTED (boat affects water, water doesn't push the boat) and 'use deforming/transform geometry' ON (else it evaluates one frame and freezes). Proxy volume = the boat VDB via re-intersect/volume-sample.

verify.cheap: (wire-only - static boat collider wired into the solver)

steps.note: before caching: delete-non-selected to KEEP only vel, vorticity, id, droplet, pscale (huge storage saving), then group_delete the now-consumed droplet group. Cache the high-res sim.

MESH FROM SCRATCH (not the shelf mesher): unpack points, blast out droplets (don't mesh them - they become whitewater), build a CUSTOM p-scale = original pscale * fit(vorticity 20..50 inverted) * fit(len(velocity) 3..8), remapped to 0.4..1 (never 0). Smaller pscale where vorticity/velocity is high -> more mesh detail there. Then VDB-from-particles at 0.6x that pscale.

key_params.pscale: dynamic: original * vorticity-mask * velocity-mask, floored at 0.4

steps.note: HOLE-FILL via narrow-band trick: the thin surface has holes where pscale eroded detail. Take the FULL-thickness VDB, erode it ~0.8 (VDB reshape - the vdb_reshape tool), then SDF-Union it UNDER the high-res mesh (high-res VDB on the LEFT so B resamples to A). Fills holes while leaving room for whitewater particles on top. VDB-convert, polyreduce (adaptive) to shed flat-area polys.

freeze one representative frame (~130) to derive the patch bounds; bound -> box -> shrink ~1m -> group-by-bounding-region (on POINTS) 'boundary' -> delete-non-boundary to trim the messy container edge back to the clean interior.

EDGE MASK (safe-VEX/VOP): per X and Z, get relative-bbox position -> a renamed ramp (rampX/rampZ, B-spline, white-black-white) -> add the two -> clamp to 1 -> bind_export 'edge'. Split into edgeX/edgeZ and flatten in two passes (avoids the diagonal interpolation artifact). Mix P.y toward 0 by the edge mask = flat rim, unchanged interior.

VDB drops attributes - transfer vel + vorticity back onto the meshed surface (clean node first to drop stray points). Cache 'flip_surface_stage_1' (cache everything incl. preroll; meshing is heavier than the sim).

RE-DISTORT the flat rim by the sim's OWN spectrum so patch edges match neighbours: save the sim spectrum via a ROP-geometry-output BGEO, then sample it with an ocean_evaluate node adding its displacement to P at the edges only (mix by 'edge'). Finally distort the whole surface back to the big-waves look (pointdeform against the hi-res big-waves grid, OR ocean_evaluate with the big-wave spectrum). pointdeform needs a HIGH-RES rest grid to capture peaks.

DISPLACE MASK + COLOR for render: remap vorticity (~0.5..10) to a displacement mask (high-freq render-time detail only where the flip is smooth, NOT where it's already rough); Cd = mix of fit(len(velocity)) + fit(vorticity) + a ramp, stored to tint the render. Cache main flip + a 10m-EXTRUDED volume (Karma/Mantra need a volume; Arnold/Redshift can use the thin surface).

variants: Neighbour patches: flatten + re-distort EVERY patch's edges by the SAME spectrum from flat-zero, so adjacent sims share identical edge points and tile seamlessly.
Non-spectrum underlying geo (modelled/scanned): you can't ocean-sample it, so use the pointdeform (rest/deformed grid) route instead - that's why both methods are taught.
Camera-aware: only simulate patches near the camera path; foreground gets its own patch (no visible tiling seam in front).
tips: DIVIDE-AND-COMBINE again: collider prep, hi-res sim, custom mesh, edge-match, render-displace are SEPARATE cached stages - each fixable without re-running the others.
The inverse-point-deform collider is the non-obvious keystone: sim on flat, collide on inverse-distorted, un-distort at render.
Custom vorticity/velocity p-scale = detail budget: dense mesh only where the water is doing something; erode the rest to whitewater particles.

TOOLS for this masterclass (all now in the catalog): ocean_evaluate (oceanevaluate::2.0 SOP — sample a SAVED spectrum BGEO to displace geo, the edge-match + big-wave-distort keystone), vdb_reshape (SDF dilate/erode/open/close by offset - the hole-fill trick), pop_wind = pop_force ftype=wind (grouped wind + swirl-size gusts), pop_drag = pop_force ftype=drag (velocity resistance).

Provenance: collider+inverse-deform ~00:00-13:00; hi-res sim + droplet wind + collision ~13:00-28:00; from-scratch mesh + custom pscale ~29:00-46:00; narrow-band hole-fill ~43:00-50:00; edge flatten (VEX ramps) ~50:00-70:00; re-distort by spectrum (ocean_evaluate) ~70:00-84:00; displacement mask + color + extrude ~84:00-88:00.
recipes.classify: high-res boat FLIP patch - inverse-deformed collider, custom-pscale mesh, edge-matched for seamless tiling
recipes.governance: the inverse point-deform is the keystone: the sim runs on the FLAT tank while the collider is inverse-distorted (rest=distorted big-waves, deformed=flat) so it un-distorts correctly at render. Recompute trail after ANY deform or the collider velocities go stale; mesh from scratch (vdb_from_particles), not the shelf mesher.

recipes.title: Large-scale RBD ice/glass destruction: clustered constraints + activation propagation + upres + secondary debris + Solaris
recipes.summary: The full hero-destruction pipeline for a huge object plowing through brittle ice: fracture -> dual glue/soft constraints tuned by rest-length + clusters -> propagating activation (only fracture what's touched) -> transform-pieces upres -> proxy+convex collider optimization -> interior-edge culling -> secondary emitted-debris sim -> snow/wind POP -> USD/Karma render with holdout mattes. (Grounded in Rebelway 'Star Destroyer Ice Destruction', frame-verified.)

steps.note: FRACTURE -> geometry + constraints out of one node. Voronoi is fine here (constraints hide the cell shapes); RBD Material Fracture (covered by sim_rbd, which wraps rbdmaterialfracture::3.0) gives richer boolean/glass-pattern detail. Scatter density sets base piece count.
the RBD Bullet solver requires PACKED pieces — pack before solving (names optional at this stage).

DUAL CONSTRAINTS: give constraints a glue name (brittle ice cracking) AND enable 'switch constraint type when broken' -> soft (the stretchy cloth-like webbing after the glue snaps). Glue strength ~18500 default; drop toward ~10 to break more easily. Soft stiffness ~1-10 controls floppiness.

CLUSTERS: glue-cluster writes an internal-strength attr (-1 default) marking intra- vs inter-cluster constraints -> control WHERE fractures concentrate (stronger inside a cluster, weaker between). WARNING: glue_cluster OVERWRITES your strength attr; copy-parameter the real strength back (or gate the cluster group on 'strength > 10') so you don't lose it.

wrangle_opportunity.why: cluster-boundary detection (A3): compare the Voronoi seed across each constraint primitive's two endpoints (primpoint -> point) to reveal inter- vs intra-cluster constraints and debug-color @Cd - the most advanced wrangle in the reference tutorial, not expressible with typed nodes.
wrangle_opportunity.consent: run via set_attrib_expr ONLY if the user has enabled allow_attrib_expr (explicit consent); otherwise propose the VEX text via vex_reference for the user to paste by hand, and EXPLAIN what it does and why (this is a teaching moment, not just an action).

steps.note: REST-LENGTH MAP: measure constraint primitive length -> 'restlength'. A safe-VEX/wrangle then removes/keeps constraints by rest_length (e.g. cull the tiny in-between ones < 1.4) and by cluster group -> an icy, non-uniform fracture map from frame 1. (VEX: minpos/prim-point pairs read the two endpoint seeds; see vex_reference.)

SOFT-BREAK sub-solver: inside the constraint network, a sub-solver breaks SOFT constraints when their 'distance' attr exceeds a threshold (~1.5-3, scene-dependent) so the stretchy bits eventually snap instead of trailing forever. Glue breaks on strength; soft breaks on distance.

verify.cheap: (wire-only - sub-solver; fire the sim to break soft constraints on distance)

wrangle_opportunity.why: soft-break threshold (A2) inside the SOP-solver: each frame, for constraints named 'soft', break (removeprim / broken group) when a solver-measured @distance exceeds a finessed ch() threshold - the 'you finesse this every time' art of destruction.
wrangle_opportunity.consent: run via set_attrib_expr with dop_target = the sopsolver, ONLY with allow_attrib_expr consent; else propose + explain the VEX for a manual paste.

steps.note: UPRES (detail without re-simming): timeshift the sim, STORE original name (critical - voronoi will rewrite it), unpack per piece, scatter + re-voronoi each piece (wrap in a compile_block for multithread speed), assemble, then transform_pieces by the STORED name so every sub-piece rides its parent's exact motion. Do the name store/transfer on POINTS.

ACTIVATION PROPAGATION: scatter points on the intra-cluster groups, colour white=active / black=inactive, transfer to pieces -> 'activate_me'. Set active=0/animated=1 globally, then a group flips active=1 only after the piece enters the propagating activation group. On the GROUND/solver enable 'Override Attributes' for active+animated so it re-checks each frame (active changes frame-to-frame as it propagates). Only fracture what the ship actually touches.

PROXY COLLIDER (optimization, ~80% of the work): shrinkwrap a matchsize'd, divided box onto the ship via a minpos() pointwrangle inside a repeat_begin/repeat_end FEEDBACK loop (~5 iterations: pointwrangle minpos -> vdb_from_polygons -> convert_volume back to polys -> normal push -> feed back). FRAME-VERIFIED: it is a minpos VEX wrangle in a for-loop, NOT a Ray node (drape mode=ray is the clean project-to-surface/shrinkwrap tool that wraps this). Retains silhouette, kills interior holes.

COLLISION PIECES: after the proxy, split top/bottom and run CONVEX DECOMPOSITION (GAP: convex_decompose) - Bullet strongly prefers convex hulls; concave collision is glitchy + uber-slow. Fills the hollow ship with sturdy convex interior pieces.

INTERIOR-EDGE CULL (only render broken faces): facet the static geo, promote name to points, fuse 2.6M->0.5M points building a shared 'id' by near-distance, detect points that MOVED vs stayed (a tiny primitive appears between a moving+static point pair) -> measure that edge length -> a max-accumulate solver locks the map to 1 (never flickers back) -> remove all interior (non-edge) geometry. Huge poly saving for long shots.

SECONDARY DEBRIS (the juice): a debris-source (the debris_source tool) on the static geo makes a p-scale/orient/angular-velocity/velocity emission map; rename per frame as name+frame+ptnum so each frame injects UNIQUE pieces. Remove by colour to thin it.

DEBRIS SOLVER (emit-RBD trick): a BLANK RBD object + a SOP-solver that each frame merges the freshly-named debris points into the sim (a 'secondary' group), inheriting velocity from points, colliding with the ship + big RBD pieces, and KILLING anything below y=-10 inside the sim (cheaper than deleting after). Spawns millions of pieces, near-fluid look.

SNOW/WIND: POP net driven by a custom 'wind tunnel' (the volume_velocity tool builds the noise-velocity wind-volume; pop_wind = pop_force ftype=wind) = box -> vdb_from_polygons -> velocity = wind_dir + dual (big+small) curl noise; NO sim needed. pcfind + array-length in a wrangle gives a neighbour-density colour -> 'wind_pocket' + 'air_resist' masks that push/resist particles (teal-snow clumping). Ship as collider; optional Axiom/pyro (sim_pyro) adds advection where velocity interaction matters.

wrangle_opportunity.why: custom particle masks (A6): a point-cloud query (pcfind + len) builds a wind-pocket / snow-density mask that scales POP forces - particle authoring a fixed force node cannot express.
wrangle_opportunity.consent: run via set_attrib_expr ONLY if the user has enabled allow_attrib_expr (explicit consent); otherwise propose the VEX text via vex_reference for the user to paste by hand, and EXPLAIN what it does and why (this is a teaching moment, not just an action).

steps.note: USD PREP (essential): DELETE the name attribute before export (else USD imports every piece separately = unworkable) - keep inside/outside as split geometry or name-from-group. usd_configure: topology attrs -> static, UV kept as 'uv' (untick the ST rename). Then export_usd to ONE file per geo (or $F4 per-frame), like a single-file Alembic.

verify.cheap: (wire-only - USD prep; verify the exported USD imports as one prim, not per-piece)

steps.note: SOLARIS RENDER: sublayer the USD caches, SOP-import the ship/glass, dome + distant light, and a GEOMETRY light copied onto the window points (copy_to_points a small light per window, nudged off the glass). Karma render; render-geometry-settings ENABLE motion blur -> velocity blur (packed/particle sims need velocity blur).

render_opportunity.why: the Solaris destruction render (sublayered caches, dome + geometry lights, velocity motion blur) is assembled WIRE-ONLY; firing the Karma render is the gated EXECUTION.
render_opportunity.propose_via: render_karma_rop (or render_usd) builds + wires the render over the sublayered USD stage; the human fires it.
render_opportunity.consent: the MCP BUILDS + WIRES the render network only (rendered:False); FIRING the render is the human's gated action - surface it as ready-to-fire via the gated_tool and explain the frame/time cost, never .render() or .execute() it.

steps.note: HOLDOUTS + PASSES: put the ship/RBD as a MATTE (holdout) so snow AB-composites cleanly; 'phantom' keeps a prim invisible-to-camera but still lighting/shadowing/colouring the snow. Split each snow layer to its own pass via a switch, driven at render time by a tiny Python 'node.parm(switch).set(n)' in the Karma ROP Scripts tab -> one ROP per pass. (Comp finish in Nuke: AI-denoise, depth-defocus, glow/anamorphic, chromatic aberration, matte-painting projection on camera-tracked cards, teal/orange grade, grain - out of Houdini scope.)

recipes.title: Seamless multi-patch ocean: tile neighbour FLIP patches by shared spectrum + velocity-advected seeding
recipes.summary: Cover a wide ocean shot with several small FLIP patches (foreground hi-res, background lo-res) that tile SEAMLESSLY: every patch is flattened at its edges and re-distorted by the SAME world-space ocean spectrum, and downstream patches are seeded by advecting their particles with the upstream patch's velocity field so the water is continuous across seams. (Grounded in SideFX 'Water FX | Stormy Seas' pt.3.)

steps.note: CAMERA FIRST: bring the shot camera in EARLY so you only sim where the camera looks. Camera shake = a Motion-Effects noise CHOP layered on the camera's translate/rotate (subtle). Sticky notes (hide-background) keep the big net readable.

each patch is a copy of the main FLIP setup (see recipe ocean_flip_boat_hires), renamed (wave_tank_side_L / top / top_center / back) and TRANSLATED into place with a little overlap. The ocean SPECTRUM is world-space + infinite, so the SAME spectrum keeps working across every patch - do NOT change it between patches; that shared spectrum is what makes seams align.

per-patch resolution to budget: foreground ~0.6 particlesep-ish hi-res, background patches coarser (res 7, size 80x50) - 'further away, you won't notice'. Give each patch enough overlap with its neighbour to hide the transition.

ADVECT-SEED downstream patches (pop_advect_volumes = pop_force ftype=advect): a POP-advect-by-volumes reads the UPSTREAM patch's named velocity field (out_vel) + surface (out_surface) and advects this patch's particles by it ('do NOT treat as wind', force ~2) so its starting motion inherits the neighbour's flow. Only needed when the wind/velocity points INTO the new patch; back patches with enough fetch can skip it.

verify.cheap: (wire-only - advect-by-volumes seeding from the upstream patch velocity field)

steps.note: SEAM MATCH (same as ocean_flip_boat_hires edge step): flatten each patch's rim, re-distort by the shared spectrum (ocean_evaluate). Because every patch flattens to zero and re-distorts by the SAME spectrum, adjacent rims land on identical points = seamless. A tiny per-patch transform (e.g. 2.31 / 0.316) dials the last bit of overlap. From camera + whitewater you can't find the seam.

variants: Order matters when advect-seeding: build the upstream (velocity-source) patch first, then advect the downstream one from its out_vel.
Pure-background patches: lower res + no advection; the shared spectrum alone tiles them acceptably.
tips: The shared WORLD-SPACE spectrum is the whole trick: one spectrum drives every patch, so flatten-to-zero + re-distort makes neighbouring rims coincide automatically.

TOOLS surfaced (now in catalog): pop_advect_volumes = pop_force ftype=advect (advect particles by a velocity VOLUME - here to seed neighbour sims, but generally: advect debris/spray/snow by a pyro/flip vel field). Plus the carried ocean_evaluate (seam re-distort).
Provenance: camera+shake+scene-org ~00:00-02:30; side-L patch + advect-seed ~02:30-10:00; seam flatten+re-distort ~10:00-13:30; top/top-center/back patches ~13:30-19:00.

When wind blows INTO a patch, advect-seed it (pop_force ftype=advect) from the upstream patch's velocity field - build the upstream patch first.

recipes.title: Surface whitewater: foam/spray/bubble states, depth-advection, foam look, wind-blown crest spray
recipes.summary: Layer believable surface whitewater (foam + spray + bubbles) onto the FLIP ocean patches: emit from vorticity, tune the three particle states, advect by depth so submerged foam rides the wave while airborne spray flies free, shape the foam (erosion/repellent cells), blow crest spray with a POP wind, then match the whitewater to the same spectrum and process p-scale for render as points or volume. (Grounded in SideFX 'Water FX | Stormy Seas' pt.4.)

steps.note: EMIT SOURCE: object-merge the FLIP compressed cache, blast surface + velocity (out_volumes/out_surface), whitewater-force emitting mainly from VORTICITY (range ~12-30; disable curvature/acceleration emission). Boost source volume res for definition. file-cache the emission. Split emission by vorticity or height range (2-3 / 3-5) if RAM-limited - whitewater merges seamlessly.

SOLVER: whitewater object+solver (gravity+buoyancy already built in). Enable STATE attributes = the foam(surface)/spray(airborne)/bubble(submerged) 0..1 blend. whitewater scale ~0.08 (>= 2x fluid particlesep), emission-amount multiplier, lifespan ~3s + variation, per-copy SEED + a little noise (freq 4). Copy the flip sim's LIMITS.

DEPTH-ADVECTION (the physics that sells it): base-advection-strength ~8 = submerged/surface foam advects with the OCEAN velocity, but once a particle flies free of the surface it keeps its OWN velocity+gravity (real physics takes over). FOAM tab: density control, stiffness ~3 (clumping) + variable-stiffness-by-depth ramp, EROSION (clumped foam lives longer, solo dies sooner; ease strength + raise preservation for salt-water persistence), REPELLENTS (the cell-pattern holes, size ~0.06-0.1m + a little noise), adhesion depth-control ~0.6 + velocity-angle threshold for when spray breaks free.

CREST SPRAY: pop-drag (pop_force ftype=drag) ~0.1 air resistance + a pop_group 'spray' (spray attr > ~0.15) + pop_wind (pop_force ftype=wind) on the spray group only (velocity ~6, +1.5 up for storm lift, swirl ~3.5) so breaking-wave spray gets torn downwind. The wind vector itself can come from the wind_field volume below.

MATCH + P-SCALE + RENDER: distort the whitewater by the SAME spectrum as the flip (ocean_evaluate - not pointdeform, for accuracy), then bind density -> fit -> export a per-point pscale (fade by depth+age; multiply base pscale ~0.35). Render as POINTS, or volume_rasterize density (particle-scale up) for extra detail + the volume-normal whitewater shader (2 stock nodes give reflection). Distant side/top/back patches: bigger pscale + form-location +0.01 above surface + lower emission.

WIND FIELD (recurring across this whole series - the volume_velocity tool): bound the render geo -> volume by size (vector 'vel') -> volume-velocity -> convert to VDB -> vector-from-scalar merge -> constant velocity (~6 fwd, +1 up) + CURL NOISE (scale ~3, size ~8-10 for big coherent swirls not per-particle jitter) -> out_wind_force. A cheap NON-simulated vector field that drives the crest-spray pop_wind (and, upstream, the snow). volume_trail visualizes it.

variants: RAM budget: 50M whitewater points ~= 120GB RAM; split emission into chunks (change seed per chunk) and merge, or sim on Linux (~30-40% less RAM than Windows same hardware).

Distant patches (side/top/back): copy-paste the setup, larger pscale so sparse particles still read, reduce emission + bubbles; orchestrate the source->sim caching with a TOP/PDG ropfetch chain (wait-for-all, all-frames-in-one-batch for sims).
Render as volume for hero close-ups (specular volume shader); as points for distance/speed.
tips: The three STATE attributes (foam/spray/bubble, 0..1 by depth) are what every downstream force keys off - enable them first.
Depth-advection is the core cheat: inside-water foam glued to ocean velocity, airborne spray on its own physics - set base-advection ~8 and the velocity-angle break threshold.

wind_field/volume_velocity is now the volume_velocity tool (Parts 2/3/4 + Star Destroyer all hand-build the same box->volume-velocity->curl-noise wind tunnel it wraps). Plus pop_drag = pop_force ftype=drag + pop_wind = pop_force ftype=wind (spray/snow forcing) and ocean_evaluate (spectrum match).

recipes.title: Spray -> mist: POP spray sim off whitewater + age-driven pscale + pyro-sparse mist emission
recipes.summary: The airborne secondary layer that sells breaking waves: emit a fast POP spray sim from the 'alive' (rising) whitewater spray, shrink each particle by age into mist, then rasterize those particles as emission for a sparse pyro smoke sim (colliding with the sails). Fast + forgiving vs the FLIP/whitewater sims. (Grounded in SideFX 'Water FX | Stormy Seas' pt.5.)

steps.note: SPRAY EMIT SOURCE: from the whitewater, keep spray attr > ~0.1, then a group-EXPRESSION selecting only RISING spray (v.y not falling) - a rising particle is 'alive/energetic' and worth emitting from; falling particles are dying, skip them. Trim container edges (timeshift+bound+group), keep only pscale+vel, cache.

POP SPRAY SIM (individual particles = fast, no neighbour solve): pop-network, birth life ~2s with NEGATIVE life-variance jitter (avoids particles appearing before the wave reaches them - cheaper than substeps), inherit velocity + a little X/Z variance.

FORCES: pop-advect-by-volumes (pop_advect_volumes = pop_force ftype=advect) reading out_wind_force (force ~2, not-as-wind) + pop_drag (pop_force ftype=drag) whose air-resistance is randomized per particle via a safe-VEX expression airresist *= fit(rand(@id),0,1 -> 0.6,1) (some particles 40% draggier - the natural look; save as a 'random ID' preset).

BOUND KILL: POP has no built-in limits - a pop_kill referencing the wind volume's centroid+size (Reference Scene Data) kills particles that LEAVE the box, plus a small random kill (~0.4) to thin. dopio pop-object particles, attribdelete to vel only.

SCALE-BY-AGE (mist logic): a wrangle sets pscale = ramp(1 - age/life) refit to ~0.002-0.0045 (born small -> grows -> fades to mist), bind_export scale; density = same ramp -> ~1..3. Age/life normalises 0..1 so the ramp shapes the whole lifespan.

wrangle_opportunity.why: age-driven pscale/opacity: drive f@pscale and Alpha from @age/@life (fit + chramp) so spray grows and fades into mist as it ages - a per-particle lifetime curve the randomize node cannot express.
wrangle_opportunity.consent: run via set_attrib_expr ONLY if the user has enabled allow_attrib_expr (explicit consent); otherwise propose the VEX text via vex_reference for the user to paste by hand, and EXPLAIN what it does and why (this is a teaching moment, not just an action).

steps.note: MIST EMITTER PREP (the point_replicate tool): delete very-young (age<0.05); DELETE-SOLO via a pcopen/pc_num_found density check (drop particles that found no neighbours - a lone point emitting smoke looks wrong); point-replicate ~30 pts/point (sphere+noise) for fuller emission; STRETCH-BY-V (wrangle P += V/-24 * rand(ptnum)) so replicated pts smear backward along velocity instead of popping from one spot; pyro_source density ~0.7 + tiny temperature ~0.02.

SPARSE MIST SMOKE: sparse pyro DOP, SOP-swap-geometry to rasterize the spray points into fields (gas-particle-to-field density_in/temperature_in/vel_in, set-ALWAYS not set-initial), gas-field-resize-DYNAMIC bounds tracking the DOP geometry (GAP: gas_resize/gasparticletofield micro-DOPs still open; sim_pyro covers the standard case). Sails as collider (distorted render-position boat + genoa, polyextrude + vdb_from_polygons + vdb_reshape erode - the vdb_reshape tool). Temperature diffusion + cooling ~6-8, dissipation, disturbance/turbulence with BIG block-size (scene scale), wind (6/10/6). Cache -> VDB convert -> split density + vector-from-scalar vel.

variants: Render mist as volume (density split) for the specular smoke look; keep it low-res - motion blur hides resolution.
No sail collision for background patches (only the foreground boat needs the vortex shaping).
tips: Emit only from RISING spray: upward v.y = energetic/alive = will actually throw mist; falling spray is dying.
Age drives everything downstream: pscale, density, and the solo-cull all key off age/life normalised 0..1.

TOOLS surfaced (now available): point_replicate (N jittered pts/point - general FX/scatter), pop_advect_volumes = pop_force ftype=advect, pop_drag = pop_force ftype=drag, vdb_reshape. Still a niche gap: gas_resize / gasparticletofield (pyro micro-DOPs).

Provenance: spray emit source (rising-only) ~00:00-07:00; POP spray sim + drag/kill ~07:00-19:00; scale-by-age pscale ~20:00-27:00; delete-solo + replicate + stretch-by-V ~28:00-39:00; sail collider ~41:00-45:00; sparse pyro mist DOP ~45:00-60:00.

recipes.title: Art-directed boat splashes: distance-emit + boat-normal velocity + wind-masked FLIP + custom whitewater volume
recipes.summary: Add controllable secondary splashes where a boat hits the waves WITHOUT over-driving the main ocean sim: emit from the hull-to-ocean contact distance, throw particles up+out along the hull normals with a keyframed per-impact multiplier, run a hi-res splash FLIP that flies free then gets wind-dragged (age-masked), and build a CUSTOM surface+velocity volume so this splash can drive its own whitewater. (Grounded in SideFX 'Water FX | Stormy Seas' pt.6.)

steps.note: EMIT AREA (do secondary splashes SEPARATELY - never over-drive the main sim, it makes artifacts): a wrangle measures hull-to-ocean XYZ distance, fit ~0.3-0.5 inverted, break with a turbulent (alligator) noise -> Cd emission mask. scatter by Cd (~150k, disable relax, tune count for water-amount variation), delete points inside the boat VDB (group-by-volume).

3-STAGE VELOCITY (the point_velocity tool): (1) add +3.5 Y (up); (2) hull NORMALS via pcopen/pcfilter (average N over radius) pushed into v so splash goes up+OUT, with a vector-to-float switch zeroing any negative-Y (splashes never go down), times a control multiplier; (3) a point_velocity curl-noise pass to break it up. KEYFRAME the multiplier per impact frame (review a boat+ocean flipbook: big splash on wave-entry frames, calm between).

wrangle_opportunity.why: boat-normal launch velocity: for each emit point push v@v along the hull normal scaled by hull speed (dot of boat velocity and N) so splashes fire off the wetted leading edge - directional emission a scalar point_velocity cannot express.
wrangle_opportunity.consent: run via set_attrib_expr ONLY if the user has enabled allow_attrib_expr (explicit consent); otherwise propose the VEX text via vex_reference for the user to paste by hand, and EXPLAIN what it does and why (this is a teaching moment, not just an action).

steps.note: SPLASH FLIP: flip object+solver hi-res (~0.01-0.03, finer than the main sim), pop_source (particle velocities, all points), negative birth jitter + small inherit. AGE the particles (required for the age mask). Volume-motion bound from the boat bbox expanded ~+5 sides / +26 back (splashes fly far). Boat as collider.

FLY-THEN-DRAG: mask-by-age (age fit 0..18/24; born=0.1 -> ~1 after ~18 frames) bind_export age_mask, then pop_advect_volumes (pop_force ftype=advect) reading the wind force scaled by age_mask (VEX: forcescale *= agemask) so a splash flies on its OWN velocity first and only gets blown downwind once airborne + pop_drag (pop_force ftype=drag) rand-by-id. Delete particles that re-enter the ocean: extrude-volume + vdb_from_polygons + vdb_reshape erode + volume_sample SDF<0 remove, in post-solve.

PSCALE + CUSTOM VOLUME: pscale/density from pcopen density (solo=small, clumped=big) * age fade (pscale 0.002-0.0085, density 1-3). Then build a whitewater-ready volume: vdb_from_particles (0.02, pscale-aware) with a 'vel' velocity field, split surface/vel.

MERGE SPLASH + FLIP FIELDS: surface = vdb_reshape dilate + vdb smooth (vdb_filter), SDF-UNION with a custom (non-eroded) flip surface. velocity = vdb_combine A-match-B (ADD, fog vdb - low-res is fine for velocity). Middle-click the merged volume -> surface + vel = the custom field the next whitewater pass emits from. Cache 'custom_volumes' (heavy per-frame). NOTE: use a CUSTOM surface/vel, not the flip compress fields - those are the FLAT pre-distort sim; you need the distorted-position fields.

variants: Keyframe the velocity multiplier off a flipbook: emphasise wave-entry impacts, calm the between-frames - art direction beats brute force.
Render the splash directly as points/whitewater, or feed the custom_volumes into ocean_whitewater_surface for a second foam layer.
tips: Golden rule: keep the MAIN ocean sim on normal velocities; layer splashes on top - cranking the main sim to force splashes makes artifacts.
up+OUT is the splash signature: +Y velocity AND hull-normal push, with negative-Y clamped to zero so nothing splashes downward.
age_mask + pop_advect_volumes = fly-then-drag: own velocity first, wind takes over after ~18 frames. This is the same wind_field/pop pattern as every other layer.

TOOLS: point_velocity (set/add v with incoming+noise modes - recurs Parts 5/6), pop_advect_volumes = pop_force ftype=advect, pop_drag = pop_force ftype=drag, vdb_reshape. vdb smooth is covered by vdb_filter.

recipes.title: Whitewater + mist from a boat-splash FLIP: velocity/age emit-selection -> whitewater source -> splash mist
recipes.summary: Turn the secondary boat-splash FLIP (from flip_boat_splash_secondary) into rendered whitewater + a light mist: select emission by speed AND youth, drive whitewater_source off the custom splash volume, process/thin the result, then spawn a fast splash-mist POP that rasterizes to smoke. Applies the ocean whitewater/mist toolset to the splash source. (Grounded in SideFX 'Water FX | Stormy Seas' pt.7.)

steps.note: EMIT SELECTION: a wrangle keeps particles with length(v) > ~4 AND age < ~0.6 (multiplicative = fast AND young; 'or' would over-select) - young fast particles throw whitewater, dying ones don't. random-delete by rand(@id) to thin (~keep 30%).
EMIT + PSCALE attrs: set 'emit' (the attr whitewater_source wants, ~0.5..10) as speed-gradient * age-fade, and pscale (~0.008..0.015), both bind_export. emit is like density but authored per-point.

SOURCE OFF CUSTOM VOLUME: input1 = the custom splash surface/vel volume (from flip_boat_splash_secondary), input2 = these emit points (whitewater_source rasterizes 'emit' into a volume internally - the modern H16+ volume emission). Emit ONLY from extra-forces (disable vorticity/curvature/accel emission since the source is explicit).

SPLASH WHITEWATER: whitewater object+solver, boat collider, age_mask -> pop_advect_volumes(wind) + pop_drag (both = pop_force, ftype=advect/drag), bound from the boat bbox, no pre-roll (start at impact frame). Foam tab: depth range ~-0.25..-1.25, variable stiffness, repellents, strength 10-12 + noise. Then process: blast bubble>0.15, delete-inside (vdb_from_polygons lo-res + vdb_reshape erode + volume_sample<0 remove - the vdb_reshape tool), pscale/density by normalised-age ramp, cull young.

SPLASH MIST: group v.x > ~4 (fast-forward particles), random-thin, pop-network + gravity + pop_advect_volumes(wind, no age_mask - they're already moving) + pop_kill on the ocean extruded-volume bound. attribrandomize pscale, set density-by-pscale, volume_rasterize density (+ velocity blur) = the mist volume.

variants: Split the whitewater sim by seed for RAM, merge later (whitewater is forgiving - overlaps read fine, no merge node needed).
Skip the mist for distant/quick shots; it's a cheap final flourish.
tips: Emit selection is speed AND youth (multiplicative). The 'emit' attribute (not density) is what whitewater_source reads.

No new gaps - this reuses the whole POP/forces + vdb_reshape cluster (pop_advect_volumes = pop_force ftype=advect, pop_drag = pop_force ftype=drag, vdb_reshape, volume_rasterize). It's the application layer of ocean_whitewater_surface + spray_to_mist_smoke onto the splash.

recipes.title: Non-simulated background ocean to the horizon: Ocean Foam whitewater + camera-distance pscale + dual-spectrum render displace
recipes.summary: Fill everything behind the simulated FLIP patches out to the horizon with ZERO simulation: generate background whitewater from the wave-cusp with Ocean Foam in camera-culled distance tiers, scale particles up with distance so sparse foam still reads, and displace both the foam and a giant render grid by the SAME two spectra (flip + big-wave) at render time. (Grounded in SideFX 'Water FX | Stormy Seas' pt.8.)

steps.note: SAVE A HI-RES SPECTRUM: duplicate the flip spectrum (linked), bump res 7->10 (same placement) and ROP-save it - the render displacement needs more detail than the sim did. You now have flip-spectrum + big-wave-spectrum BGEOs.

BG WHITEWATER (no sim): Ocean Foam generates foam from the wave CUSP of the small (flip) spectrum only - the big geo doesn't make whitewater. Two distance tiers (e.g. 50-200m + 200-600m), CAMERA-CULLED (particle density falls off with distance; cull outside a slightly-wider-than-camera frustum), downsample the ocean-evaluate for the far tier. NOTE: ocean_foam here needs the SOLVER-tab params (life_expectancy ~1.5, drift_rate = advect-by-ocean-velocity, foam_density min/max ~3..10, camera+distance cull, downsample) - PARAM-DEEPENING candidate; current ocean_foam only exposes amount/threshold.

PSCALE BY CAMERA DISTANCE: object-merge the camera origin (Into This Object), copy a sphere to it, then a wrangle measures XYZ distance to camera and fits it (near=1, far=3) * base pscale - distant foam gets bigger so sparse points still fill. Do it per tier (near tier fits 70..200, far 200..600); the tier boundaries' pscales must match (0.13 = end of near = start of far).

DUAL-SPECTRUM DISPLACE (ocean_evaluate - LOAD-BEARING here): two ocean_evaluate nodes sample the flip spectrum AND the big-wave spectrum from their saved BGEOs (position->position, time->time) and ADD both displacements to P. Same technique as the sim edge-match, now for the whole background. Add a density attr for the foam (fit pscale -> 1..3).

RENDER GRID: a big grid (~5000x5000, light geometry), camera-centred with just enough horizon overlap, displaced by the SAME two spectra at render time, volume-extrude ~10m down for a Karma volume. This is the actual ocean surface from mid-ground to horizon - the FLIP patches sit on top.

variants: Storage-limited: drop whitewater counts + scene size; the CONCEPTS carry - just raise foam pscale so fewer particles still fill the frame.

recipes.title: Vellum cloth sails on a moving rig: attach-to-geometry + POP wind + UV-transfer restore
recipes.summary: Simulate boat sails (mainsail + genoa) as Vellum cloth pinned to the animated rigging: isolate the thin sail by material path, remesh adaptively, attach it to the boat's tracks/cables with a max-distance attach constraint, drive it with the SAME POP wind as the FX, then restore the clean render UVs (lost in the remesh) via UV-transfer + pointdeform. steps.note: ISOLATE by material path (not point count - so vellum post-process thickness deletions don't break it): blast the mainsail + its ATTACH geometry (sail track, boom, cables/halyard) off the render boat. REMESH the sail ADAPTIVE (not uniform) - more subdivision where the cloth deforms most (belly vs the flatter flag areas), fewer elsewhere; the mesh density drives the constraint/deformation quality. (Genoa: uniform ~15 for a stiffer, more consistent headsail.)
CLOTH constraints: vellum-cloth on the sail, lower the damping ratio for a big object (bleeds the stiff-constraint jitter). Genoa gets higher stiffness (it's pressurised/taut vs the flapping main).

ATTACH TO RIG (GAP: vellum_attach): a Vellum-attach-to-geometry constraint pins the sail edge to the track/cable geometry (2nd input = the rest rig). Enable MAX DISTANCE ~0.1m (only points within 10cm attach - stops the whole sail flying), attach on the animation start frame (~48), no sliding. This is distinct from the cloth material constraint.

WIND: POP forces are compatible with Vellum - a pop_wind (pop_force ftype=wind, ~8/8 + gust amplitude + swirl-scale 4) + pop_drag (pop_force ftype=drag), the SAME wind as the ocean FX so the sail and spray agree. Cross-domain confirmation that the POP/forces cluster serves cloth too.

Also animate the boom rotation (rig HDA param) - the attach lines follow. Mirror-side sails: flip transforms positive before caching.

recipes.title: Foreground rain/spray across the lens: camera-frustum emit + sparse pyro mist + POP rain advected by it + 3-layer matte render
recipes.summary: The in-your-face foreground layer: spray/rain streaking across the low camera. Emit only inside the camera frustum with a noise-broken density (for depth), run a sparse pyro MIST sim, then a fast POP rain sim advected by that mist's velocity, and render in 3 matte-separated layers. (Grounded in SideFX 'Water FX | Stormy Seas' pt.11.)

steps.note: CAMERA-FRUSTUM EMIT REGION (GAP: volume_from_camera): a volume-from-camera (near ~2m, far ~50m, slightly padded) bounds emission to what the lens sees; two timeshifts (first+last anim frame) + bound capture the whole camera move; transform up (no rain under water); blast the upwind side face. Remesh dense (needs resolution to store the noise).

NOISE DENSITY FOR DEPTH: a wrangle stores an anti-aliased noise (glass frequency ~0.12, animated $T and $T*0.5) -> density, clamped 0..1. The negative-space chunks (some emission near, some far, gaps between) are what give the foreground DEPTH instead of a flat wall of particles. Scatter by density (with a density-scale so counts stay stable as the noise animates).

SEED VELOCITY (the point_velocity tool): +8/8 initial (the project-wide wind range) + a coherent big-scale noise (scale ~8, not per-particle). pyro_source adds a touch of temperature (~0.02) for lift.

SPARSE MIST: sparse pyro (smoke object res ~0.8), gas-particle-to-field (density/temp/vel, set-ALWAYS) + gas-resize-dynamic tracking the DOP geometry to a camera-frustum max-bound. Temperature diffusion ~0.3 (lets it fall, not just rise), NO dissipation (rain mustn't vanish mid-air), disturbance big-block + turbulence + wind 10/7. Cache density+vel; convert VDB, split, vector-from-scalar. Delete mist inside the ocean (flip render-vol as fog + volume_sample>0).

POP RAIN (advected by the mist - richer than the noise wind_field): pop-network + gravity + pop_advect_volumes reading the MIST velocity field (out_mist_vel) + pop_kill (outside frustum bound AND inside ocean) + pop_drag. attribrandomize pscale ~0.005-0.025. ~4-5M pts, fast. Cache with pre-roll.

3-LAYER MATTE RENDER: render (a) everything EXCEPT foreground mist/rain, (b) the mist+rain WITH the boat as a MATTE (holdout) so it cuts particles behind the boat - ocean particles were already deleted so the ocean needn't be a matte, (c) the background ocean - as SEPARATE passes comp'd together. Rain shader = standard-surface glass (IOR 1.3, low diffuse, specular); mist = volume density.

recipes.title: Wide distance ocean shot: scattered real-whitewater + per-point spectrum instancing to break tiling (mask-locked hero area)
recipes.summary: Cover a huge distant ocean without a 300m sim: recycle REAL simulated whitewater by scattering + copy-to-points onto a displaced grid (richer than cusp foam), and defeat the visible tiling of a repeating spectrum by INSTANCING a different ocean spectrum per scatter point - while a contribution/suppression MASK keeps the hero (boat) area on the same spectrum as the sim. (Grounded in SideFX 'Water FX | Stormy Seas' pt.13.)

steps.note: RECYCLE WHITEWATER: merge existing whitewater patches, random-thin (group-expression by rand(@id)) to an even ~1M, delete old pscale/density, then FADE pscale+density toward the tile edges (freeze-frame bound + bbox-relative rampX*rampZ) so scattered copies blend; density-search pscale (pcopen) so clumps read bigger. This real sim foam has motion cusp-foam lacks.

SCATTER + ALIGN: flatten Y + center to origin + ray onto the render grid; scatter ~thousands of points (relax iterations ~15, large relax radius ~100m for even spread), then scatter-align to add per-point rotation (0-13deg) + scale (0.9-1.2) variation.

COPY WHITEWATER TO POINTS: copy_to_points the recycled-whitewater chunk onto the scattered points -> a wide field of REAL whitewater, each copy displaced differently by the grid so it doesn't read as repetition. Then displace by spectrum (below).

SPECTRUM INSTANCING = anti-tiling (GAP: ocean_spectrum #294 needs its POINT-INSTANCING subsystem + wave-instancing param exposed - the exact pointwave params excluded when it was first built): scatter points on the ocean grid, SPLIT them in half, instance a DIFFERENT spectrum (different seed/amp/wind) per half via wave-instancing radius, merge. Each point carries its own spectrum -> the repeat pattern of a single tiled spectrum is broken across a wide camera. Do it for BOTH the big-wave and the mid(flip) spectrum (smaller grid 80 = repeats more, needs more instancing).

HERO-AREA MASK LOCK (GAP: ocean_spectrum mask input - contribution/suppression): the boat area must keep the SAME spectrum as the sim (so the animation matches). Build a fog-VDB mask from a bound-sphere around the boat (bound->sphere->vdb_from_polygons fog + volume_sample + a volume-VOP distance-gradient ramp), feed it to the spectrum's MASK input as CONTRIBUTION for the hero spectrum and SUPPRESSION for the instanced-variation spectra. Result: constant hero spectrum in the centre, tiling-broken variation everywhere else. Save the combined spectra BGEOs.

variants: Even wider: raise the wave-instancing scatter count until flat (un-instanced) gaps disappear (needs enough points that every spectrum tile is covered).
Cheaper still: fall back to ocean_background_horizon's cusp Ocean Foam for the very far background where tiling won't be read.

DISTANCE-SHOT RENDER (pt.14 continuation): distort the scattered whitewater by BOTH spectra (flip*0.4 + big), recycle the rain/mist positioned for the new camera, render via solaris_ocean_render_assembly. Add a KARMA FOG BOX (GAP: karma_fog_box - atmospheric fog volume: density/shadow-density/scattering-phase/tint, positioned+scaled+rotated to sit on the horizon) for night haze. Comp: shuffle a camera-space depth AOV ('tap' float render-var) and grade through it (gain-down on the depth mask) to sink the background into fog + a boat roto-mask grade.
tips: Two anti-repetition wins here: (1) scatter REAL whitewater (varied motion) instead of cusp foam; (2) instance a different SPECTRUM per point so a single tiled spectrum never repeats across the frame.

ACTION FOR THE TOOL: ocean_spectrum (#294) was built WITHOUT its point-instancing subsystem (dopointrad/pointamp/wave-instancing) and WITHOUT the mask input - this recipe proves both are needed for wide shots. Param-deepen #294 to expose wave-instancing + a mask(contribution/suppression) input.
