Use list_working_dir (pattern='*.png' / '*.jpg') to discover whether the reference is actually on the Houdini disk before deciding.
Single view has NO true depth: you are matching silhouette + proportion, not reconstructing metric geometry. For metric accuracy use a scan (capture_scan_to_mesh).
Build every element under its own OUT_ null before assembling - it keeps the graph legible and re-runnable.
One element per /obj, verified before the next - do not batch a multi-object scene. Position is a discrete FINAL step after every element is confirmed.
Inspect with capture_ui panel=viewport (frame first) - cheap and inline. snapshot fires an MPlay/ROP export and costs context; save it for the final beauty check.

recipes.classify: scan / point cloud / LiDAR / photogrammetry -> a clean, meshed, exportable model
recipes.title: Scan -> clean mesh: import a point cloud, clean it, add normals, then mesh and repair
recipes.summary: The capture / scan-to-model lane: take a raw scan (.ply/.las/.laz), remove outliers, compute normals (scans have none), optionally segment flat facades for buildings, then surface it to polygons, repair, and export. Every step plants an OUT_ null so counts are readable and the chain is re-runnable.
recipes.governance: Scans have NO normals - point_normals is a HARD prereq before meshing (meshing without normals gives a blobby / inside-out surface). despeckle BEFORE meshing (outliers become spikes). voxel_size on mesh_pointcloud is the master cost/detail dial: too small = huge poly count + slow, so probe mem first. For buildings run segment_planar so walls stay flat facades instead of lumpy blobs.

steps.note: Load the scan as points. downsample if it is huge; recenter to origin for a sane working scale.
Remove isolated outlier points (scan noise / flyers) before meshing so they do not become spikes.

key_params.min_nbrs: min neighbors to keep a point

verify.cheap: read_geo_stats @OUT_clean_cloud (expect a modest drop from OUT_raw_cloud)

wrangle_opportunity.why: statistical outlier cull: for each point measure mean neighbour distance via pcopen/pcfilter and remove points beyond N sigma - a density-aware scan cleanup the despeckle node's fixed threshold cannot express.
wrangle_opportunity.consent: run via set_attrib_expr ONLY if the user has enabled allow_attrib_expr (explicit consent); otherwise propose the VEX text via vex_reference for the user to paste by hand, and EXPLAIN what it does and why (this is a teaching moment, not just an action).

steps.note: Compute point normals - a HARD prereq for meshing. radius_m must match the scan's point spacing (too small = no neighbors = no normals).
OPTIONAL (buildings/architecture): segment the cloud into planar regions so facades fit flat planes instead of organic blobs. Skip for organic subjects (rock, tree, terrain).
Surface the cloud to polygons. voxel_size is the detail/cost dial - probe mem first on large scans.
Fill holes, remove non-manifold junk, keep the largest shell. Use quad_remesh instead for a clean animation-ready quad mesh.
Optionally assign a USD material first, then write the finished model to the working dir (confined).

key_params.output: the export path (read-confined, in the working dir)

verify.cheap: read_geo_stats @OUT_clean_mesh + confirm the written file exists

rop_opportunity.why: the cleaned, meshed scan is ready to write; exporting the raw geometry stream (points/mesh + attributes) to a confined file is a gated file WRITE.
rop_opportunity.propose_via: export_geometry_raw builds + wires the raw geometry-export ROP; the human fires the write.
rop_opportunity.consent: the MCP BUILDS + WIRES the output ROP only; WRITING the file is the human's gated action - surface it as ready-to-fire via the gated_tool and explain what/where it writes, never .render()/.execute() it.

variants: LiDAR .las/.laz: use las_import (classification / intensity / color / max_points) instead of import_pointcloud.
Building / architectural scan: keep segment_planar so facades fit flat (the clean architectural-scan lane).
Heavy scan: downsample on import (or las_import max_points) BEFORE meshing to stay inside the mem budget.
Animation-ready retopo: quad_remesh instead of mesh_repair for uniform quads.
Assign a material: assign_usd_material before export_geometry, or export raw and shade downstream.
tips: Verify point counts at EVERY null - a scan that loses 90% of its points at despeckle had bad outlier settings.
No normals = bad mesh. point_normals is not optional for real scans.
voxel_size too small will blow the poly budget and stall - probe mem, start coarse, refine.

recipes.classify: organic / soft / concave vessel - bowls, vases, cups, pots, hollow rounded props (lathe / revolve, not boolean)
recipes.title: Concave vessel: revolve a profile into a bowl/vase shell, bevel the rim, clean
recipes.summary: The organic/soft modeling row. A vessel is a lathe form: draw an open profile curve in one plane, revolve it around an axis into a shell, bevel the rim so it reads as thickness, and clean. No booleans, so none of the analytic-prim traps of hard-surface modeling.
recipes.governance: A revolved profile is a SHELL, open at the top - correct for a bowl/vase; do NOT try to make it solid. Keep the profile a simple OPEN curve in one plane (draw in XY, revolve around Y). Bevel the rim so it has apparent thickness. Concave interior is fine for a hull - it is not a boolean.

steps.note: Draw the vessel's cross-section as an open profile in the XY plane (the outline of one side, from base to rim).
Revolve the profile around the Y axis into a shell of revolution (the bowl/vase body).

wrangle_opportunity.why: a plain revolve is radially symmetric - a 'ball with a dimple'. A believable organic form (an apple with 5 calyx lobes at the base, a top-heavy profile, slight asymmetry; a hand-thrown pot with a wobble) needs measured per-point displacement radius += f(angle, height) that no typed SOP parameter can express. This is the point where an organic revolve stops being a lathe and needs a wrangle.
wrangle_opportunity.propose_via: vex_reference topic=geometry (functions=atan2, length, fit, cos, smooth) - propose the profile-shaping snippet as TEXT for the user to read and paste; explain the lobe count / falloff so it is a teaching moment, not a black box.
wrangle_opportunity.consent: run via set_attrib_expr ONLY if the user has enabled allow_attrib_expr (explicit consent); otherwise propose the VEX text via vex_reference for the user to paste by hand, and EXPLAIN what it does and why. The gated lane refusing by default is the boundary working as designed - do not try to route around it.

steps.note: Bevel the rim edge so the lip reads as real thickness (no CG edge is perfectly sharp).
Fuse coincident points along the revolve seam and fix normals before export.

variants: Thick-walled vessel: revolve a double profile (outer wall down, up the inside) so it has real wall thickness.
Tube/pipe base: create_primitive tube (solid=false) instead of a hand-drawn revolved profile.

Organic lumpy prop (rock, fruit): start from a subdivided create_primitive sphere/box and soft-deform, or mesh_pointcloud from a scan - this recipe is the fallback lane for round/organic forms. For fruit-style asymmetry (calyx lobes, top-heavy profile) the revolve step carries a wrangle_opportunity.

Look-dev: for the FINAL surface use a real material (assign_material / quickmaterial / assign_usd_material + material_graph_create), not a flat Cd. A Cd attribute (attribute_create / set_color) is fine as a quick stand-in tint while blocking out, but it reads as flat paint - name the material path for the finished look.
tips: Draw the profile in ONE plane; a profile that wanders off-plane makes the revolve self-intersect.
Revolve around the axis the profile sits BESIDE, not through - the profile should not cross the axis.
Bevel AFTER revolve; weld the seam in clean or the rim shows a crack.
Flat Cd is a blocking stand-in; assign a real material (assign_material / quickmaterial) for the final look.
Inspect with capture_ui panel=viewport (frame first) - cheap and inline; reserve snapshot (MPlay/ROP export) for the final beauty check.

recipes.classify: compose a multi-object scene from scratch - a still life, a set of props, set dressing, a kit of parts (several distinct objects built + materialed + positioned together, no reference photo)
recipes.title: Scene assembly: build each object in its own /obj, material it, then position as a discrete final step
recipes.summary: The multi-object composition row - the discipline behind the fruit-bowl drive, generalized. Build each element ONE AT A TIME in its OWN /obj, verify it, give it a real material, and only AFTER every element is individually confirmed do you position them in world space as a discrete final pass. This recipe orchestrates OTHER recipes (it is a map, not a single build); the non-reference sibling of image_to_3d_spine.
recipes.governance: The load-bearing discipline (a blind agent has no one to coach it): build + verify ONE element per object, each in its OWN /obj - do NOT batch a whole multi-object scene in a single pass, it fails silently and you lose track of what broke. Give each finished element a REAL material (assign_material / quickmaterial), not a flat Cd, before moving on. Positioning in world space is a DISCRETE FINAL step, done only after EVERY element is individually confirmed - never position while still modeling. Run layout_nodes on a cadence (fresh nodes spawn stacked). Plant a named OUT_<element> null at each finished element and object_merge the NULLS, never raw nodes. INSPECT with capture_ui panel=viewport (frame first) - cheap; reserve snapshot for a final beauty check. READ THE SCENE BACK (read_network /obj for the object list + wiring, read_geo_stats per element) instead of trusting your memory of it - the scene is external memory.

steps.note: Decompose the scene into its distinct elements: list them (a bowl + 3 apples + an orange + a leaf), estimate each element's real-world size, and note the intended layout (what sits where). No MCP call - you reason first so the build order + final positions are decided up front.

For EACH element, ONE at a time: recipe_reference classify=<element> -> its entry_recipe (a bowl -> concave_vessel, a hard-surface prop -> model_hardsurface_kit, foliage -> proc_biome_scatter), build it in its OWN /obj, and plant a named OUT_<element> null on the result. Verify THIS element before starting the next.

key_params.per_element: classify -> entry_recipe -> build in its own /obj -> OUT_<element> null
key_params.one_at_a_time: confirm each element before the next; do NOT batch

steps.note: Give each finished element a real material (a red principled for an apple, a glazed ceramic for the bowl). A flat Cd is a blocking stand-in only - the material path is the finished look.

key_params.material: a real material per element (principled / quickmaterial), not flat Cd

verify.cheap: capture_ui panel=viewport (frame the element) - it reads as a surface, not flat paint

steps.note: THE FINAL DISCRETE STEP: once every element is built + materialed + confirmed, position each one in world space to its planned spot (a bowl at origin, apples arranged inside/around). Do this LAST - positioning mid-build makes it impossible to tell a modeling error from a placement error.

key_params.t: world-space position per element (from the plan)
key_params.when: AFTER all elements confirmed - a discrete final pass

verify.cheap: capture_ui panel=viewport (frame all) - elements sit where the plan says

steps.note: Assemble: pull the placed OUT_<element> nulls into a composed result by REFERENCE (object_merge the null paths, never the raw producing nodes), so re-runs and edits upstream stay stable.

key_params.reference: the null, never the raw node

steps.note: Final legibility check: read_network /obj to confirm every element object exists, is displayed, and is named as planned; layout_nodes any stacked network; then capture_ui the framed result. The structural read is your durable map - especially across a context compaction.

key_params.path: /obj (object list + display flags), or /obj/<element> to read a chain's wiring

verify.milestone_check: capture_ui panel=viewport (the composed scene reads correctly)

variants: With a reference photo of the scene -> image_to_3d_spine (adds a camera + plate + register-to-photo); scene_assembly is the no-reference version.
Kit of identical parts (bolts, tiles) -> build ONE, then proc_scatter_instance / copy_to_points to place many, instead of one /obj each.
Set dressing on a surface -> build the hero props here, scatter the small filler with proc_biome_scatter.
tips: One element per /obj, verified, before the next - batching a whole scene in one pass is the #1 way a multi-object build goes wrong.
Position is a FINAL discrete step - never move things while still modeling them.
Material each element for real (assign_material), not a flat Cd tint.
read_network /obj is your external memory - read the scene back instead of assuming what you built.
layout_nodes on a cadence; reference OUT_ nulls, never raw nodes.

recipes.classify: model an object precisely from orthographic reference plates - front/side/top photos or a blueprint (the car-modeler / hard-surface workflow: pin plates on cameras, model against the silhouette)
recipes.title: Reference-plate modeling: pin ortho plates on cameras, model against the silhouette, verify through the plate
recipes.summary: ONE way to do precise reference-driven modeling - the workflow a car / hard-surface modeler actually uses (adapt freely). Pin your reference images (front/side/top, or a blueprint) as backgrounds on ORTHOGRAPHIC cameras, set scale from a known dimension, then build geometry so its silhouette matches each plate, checking by looking THROUGH each plate camera. This is single-view's precise cousin: several orthographic views instead of one, so you get real proportion in every axis instead of guessing depth.
recipes.governance: This is a guide, not a spec - there are many ways to model to reference; this is a reliable one. Plates only register if the camera is ORTHOGRAPHIC (projection=ortho) and its orthowidth matches the plate's real-world width - a perspective camera never lines up. Match resx/resy to each plate's pixel aspect. One camera PER view (front looks down -Z, side down -X, top down -Y), named CONTROL_cam_front etc. Set SCALE first from a known dimension in a plate (a 4.5 m car -> orthowidth ~5 m) so everything is to real scale. Model against the SILHOUETTE (match the outline) - ortho plates give you proportion + profile, not surface microdetail; cross-reference two views to place depth. Verify by looking THROUGH each plate camera (set_view_camera) and snapshotting: your geometry's outline should sit on the plate's outline. Plates are READ-CONFINED (must live in the working dir - list_working_dir to find them); a user upload that isn't on disk can't be pinned (verify against your own read of the reference instead).

steps.note: Find the reference plates on disk and confirm which views you have (front / side / top / three-quarter). If the reference is a user upload not yet in the working dir, it can't be pinned as a plate - fall back to verifying against your own read of it.

One ORTHOGRAPHIC camera per view, each with its plate pinned as background. projection=ortho; orthowidth = the subject's real width; resx/resy match the plate aspect; t/r orient the view (front down -Z, side down -X, top down -Y). Name each CONTROL_cam_<view>.

verify.cheap: set_view_camera CONTROL_cam_front - the plate fills the frame as backdrop

steps.note: Block out the main masses to the silhouette: drop primitives / a scale reference sized from the plate (a box the length+height of the car) so proportion is locked before detail. Look through CONTROL_cam_front / _side while placing (set_view_camera) so the blockout sits on the outline.

verify.cheap: snapshot @CONTROL_cam_front over the plate - the blockout matches the overall silhouette

steps.note: Trace the key profiles from the plates as curves (the side profile, a section through the body), drawn to sit on the plate outline in its view - these drive the surfaces. One curve per meaningful section.

key_params.points: traced from the plate silhouette in one ortho view
key_params.closed: false for an open profile, true for a section loop

verify.cheap: snapshot @CONTROL_cam_side - the curve lies on the plate outline

steps.note: Build surface from the profiles (sweep a cross-section along a profile, or revolve a radial profile, or polyextrude a traced outline) so the form matches the plates in every view. Cross-reference two ortho views to set depth the single plate can't show. Refine, position with transform.

key_params.note: sweep/revolve/polyextrude per part - whichever fits the form

verify.cheap: snapshot @CONTROL_cam_front AND @CONTROL_cam_side - the surface silhouette matches BOTH plates

steps.note: Legibility + final check: read_network /obj to confirm the cameras + parts exist and are named; snapshot through each plate camera one more time to confirm the whole model registers. The structural read is your durable map across a compaction.

key_params.path: /obj (cameras + parts), or /obj/<part> for a chain's wiring

variants: Front + side pair only (no top) - enough for many props; add top for symmetry-critical or complex forms.
A blueprint / orthographic technical drawing instead of photos - better than photos (already ortho, no lens distortion).
Organic form implied by the silhouette (muscle, asymmetry) -> the gated set_attrib_expr wrangle for measured detail the plate can't parametrize.
A single perspective photo (not ortho views) -> image_to_3d_spine instead - one view, silhouette + proportion only.
Dense hero asset already modelled elsewhere -> don't remodel; import it (import_geo / fbx_archive_import) and use plates only to check scale/placement.
tips: Ortho camera + orthowidth = the real width, or the plate will not register - a perspective camera never lines up.
Model the SILHOUETTE first; depth comes from cross-referencing two views, not from one plate.
Look THROUGH the plate camera (set_view_camera) while modelling - that is the whole method.
Plates must be in the working dir (list_working_dir to find them); an AI-container upload can't be pinned.
This is one route - Houdini has many; adapt the tools (sweep vs revolve vs polyextrude) to the form.

recipes.classify: import an existing 3D asset / model file (FBX / OBJ / USD / Alembic) and organize it - inspect its parts, name them, confirm scale - ready to rig / modify / place (NOT a scan, NOT modeling from scratch)
recipes.title: Asset ingest: import a model file, inspect + organize + name its parts, confirm scale
recipes.summary: ONE way to bring an existing modeled asset into Houdini ready to work on (adapt freely). FORMAT-GATE first: Houdini reads .obj/.fbx/.abc/.usd/.bgeo/.stl/.ply RELIABLY; a .dae (COLLADA) reads through the File SOP but often INCOMPLETELY for a complex/instanced asset (VERIFY the poly count against the source); the proprietary .max / .blend / .c4d / .3ds must be CONVERTED first, OUTSIDE Houdini (Blender / Assimp). Always verify the import is COMPLETE, not just non-erroring. Then import (fbx_archive_import keeps materials + separates named parts; import_geo for a single mesh; import_alembic / usd_import for cached/USD), read the structure back (read_network / read_geo_stats), confirm SCALE, and organize + name the parts so downstream rig / modify / place stays legible. You are NOT remodelling a good asset - you preserve it and work from it.
recipes.governance: FORMAT-GATE (do this FIRST): Houdini 21's File SOP reads .obj/.bgeo/.fbx/.stl/.ply/.geo natively, plus .abc (Alembic) and .usd via their own SOPs, and it CAN read .dae (COLLADA) through the File SOP, but UNRELIABLY for a complex/instanced asset: on a real 93 MB instanced architectural .dae the bare File SOP imported only ~11.6k polys (a base + a few beams, NO material groups) - it dropped the whole instanced building. So treat FBX / USD / OBJ / Alembic as the RELIABLE formats; for a .dae, either use Houdini's GUI File>Import>COLLADA (not bridge-scriptable) or CONVERT it in Blender to .fbx/.usd first (Blender resolves the full COLLADA scene graph + instances). The proprietary app formats .max (3ds Max), .blend (Blender), .c4d (Cinema 4D), .3ds likewise must be CONVERTED to .fbx/.obj/.usd/.abc outside Houdini first (Blender: File>Import then File>Export; or Assimp: `assimp export in.max out.fbx`), a human hand-off, NOT a bridge step. AFTER any import, VERIFY the result is complete - read_geo_stats poly count + a snapshot against the source image; a suspiciously low count or missing parts means the format/importer dropped geometry (re-import via a converted FBX/USD). Confirm the format with list_working_dir. HEAVY-ASSET GUARD: a big mesh (that 93 MB .dae included) can be heavy - check mem / the governor envelope first, and load PACKED (import_geo include_prim_types, or fbx pack) so it comes in as ONE flat-memory packed prim and the viewport survives (a packed prim shows as its bounding box until you unpack it - unpack when you need the real parts/polys). Pick the importer by format + intent: fbx_archive_import for a rigged / multi-material asset (separates + names parts, carries materials + skeleton); import_geo for OBJ/COLLADA/STL/PLY (+ any .mtl); import_alembic / usd_import for a cache. After import: read_network /obj to see what came in, read_geo_stats for counts + attributes, confirm SCALE (a building is tens of metres, not 0.01 or 100000), then unpack + node_organize + name the parts and plant OUT_ nulls on the ones you'll rig / place.

steps.note: Find the asset, its FORMAT, and its sidecar files (textures, .mtl). recursive=true to see the source/ + textures/ layout. Named material textures (_mat_brick, _mat_roof...) tell you the asset is already separated into material groups - your future parts.

key_params.pattern: '*' first, then '*.fbx'/'*.obj'/'*.usd'/'*.abc' to spot the native file

verify.cheap: list_working_dir shows the model file + textures

steps.note: Is the model a Houdini-native geometry file (.obj/.fbx/.abc/.usd/.bgeo/.stl/.ply)? If YES continue. If it is .dae/.max/.blend/.c4d/.3ds, STOP: it must be converted to .fbx/.obj/.usd/.abc OUTSIDE Houdini first (Blender import->export, or `assimp export in.dae out.fbx`). Do NOT attempt a direct import - it fails, or hangs on a huge file. Surface this to the user as the next action.

verify.cheap: (reason over the extension - native, or converted)

steps.note: Check RAM + VRAM headroom before importing a big asset - a multi-GB mesh can freeze the viewport. If tight, plan a PACKED load.

verify.cheap: mem - headroom for the asset size

steps.note: Import by format + intent: fbx_archive_import for a rigged / multi-material asset (separates + names parts, carries materials + skeleton); import_geo (+ include_prim_types for packed) for a single OBJ/mesh; import_alembic / usd_import for a cache. Confined to the working dir.

See what actually came in: read_network /obj for the object(s) + read_network the imported geo for its SOP structure / parts; read_geo_stats for point/prim counts + attributes (material/name/path groups). This is where you learn the part breakdown (the _mat_* groups) you'll rig / place.

verify.cheap: read_network + read_geo_stats (include_prim_types) - parts + material groups visible

steps.note: Confirm SCALE (a building = tens of metres; if it imported at 0.01 or 100000, transform to real scale as a discrete step), then organize + NAME the parts / material groups and plant OUT_<part> nulls on the ones you'll rig or place. Legible + named = ready for vehicle_rig / scene_assembly / placement.

key_params.scale: transform to real-world scale if the import unit was wrong

verify.cheap: read_network /obj - parts named, scale sane; capture_ui panel=viewport

variants: Rigged character / vehicle FBX -> fbx_archive_import (keeps skeleton + skin + materials) -> then vehicle_rig / a KineFX lane.
Single OBJ mesh (+ .mtl) -> import_geo; USD / Alembic cache -> usd_import / import_alembic.

A .dae that imports INCOMPLETELY (low poly count / missing parts - a complex instanced COLLADA), or a .max/.blend/.c4d/.3ds -> CONVERT in Blender to .fbx/.usd first (Blender resolves the COLLADA scene graph + instances the File SOP drops), then re-enter here.
Just checking scale / placement of a hero asset -> import PACKED (include_prim_types) so it stays light.
A scan / point cloud (.ply/.las/.laz), not a modelled asset -> capture_scan_to_mesh instead.
tips: VERIFY the import is COMPLETE, not just non-erroring - read_geo_stats poly count + a snapshot vs the source image. FBX/USD/OBJ/ABC are reliable; a .dae reads via the File SOP but often INCOMPLETELY for instanced assets (a 93 MB temple came in as ~11.6k polys with no parts) - convert a complex .dae in Blender; .max/.blend/.c4d/.3ds must be converted.
Big asset? Check mem, load PACKED (include_prim_types / fbx pack) so the viewport survives.
Confirm SCALE after import - a wrong unit makes a building 1 cm or 100 km.
Named material textures (_mat_brick, _mat_roof...) are your part breakdown - the groups you rig / place.
Don't remodel a good asset - ingest preserves it; you rig / modify / place from here.

recipes.classify: scene organization / legibility / naming - make the node graph readable + re-runnable (the landmark convention)
recipes.title: Nulls & naming: build -> name -> null -> read-back (the scene is external memory)
recipes.summary: The load-bearing construction habit behind every other recipe. Plant a NAMED null at each meaningful result so downstream references target a stable NAME (not a raw node that moves), and read it back to confirm what it carries. This is how a driving agent keeps a big graph legible and re-runnable instead of losing track of it.
recipes.governance: OUT_<name> = a stable RESULT handle (downstream object_merge/refs target the NAME, so inserting nodes above never breaks them). IN_<name> = an external-geo ENTRY. CONTROL = a null holding driver parms / a spare input. Plant a null at every branch result; reference nulls, NEVER raw nodes. The scene graph is your external memory - read it back with read_geo_stats instead of trusting your assumptions about what a node produced.

steps.note: After a meaningful result, drop a null and name it OUT_<what-it-is> (OUT_boolean, OUT_clean_mesh). That name is now the stable handle for this branch.

key_params.input: the node whose result you want to pin
key_params.name: OUT_<descriptive>

steps.note: Downstream (or in another network) pull the branch in by REFERENCING the OUT_ null's path. Because you target the name, inserting nodes above OUT_<name> does not break this reference.

key_params.note: reference the null, never the raw producing node

steps.note: Read the null back: confirm point/prim counts and attributes are what you think they are before you build on top of it. The scene is external memory - verify it, don't assume it.

variants: CONTROL null: park driver parameters (a global scale, a seed) on a CONTROL null and reference them, so one edit propagates.
assign_name / a group can carry intent alongside the null when a bare name is not enough.
Every other recipe's `landmark` field IS this convention - the OUT_ names in flip_splash, capture_scan_to_mesh, etc. are these nulls.
tips: Name the null for WHAT IT IS, not the node that made it (OUT_clean_mesh, not OUT_meshrepair1).
One null per branch result - that is what makes assembly (object_merge several OUT_ nulls) legible.
If you cannot say what a null carries, read_geo_stats it before continuing.

recipes.classify: graph capture / screenshot / documentation - the node graph is unreadable until it is laid out
recipes.title: Organize before capture: layout -> frame -> capture (never screenshot a stacked graph)
recipes.summary: A UI/inspection recipe, not a geometry build. Freshly created nodes spawn stacked and overlapping, so a raw capture_ui of the network is unreadable. Lay the graph out, frame the region that matters, THEN capture.
recipes.governance: Nodes spawn stacked - a raw capture of a fresh network is an unreadable pile. ALWAYS layout_nodes (and frame the region) BEFORE any graph capture. This recipe produces an IMAGE for the operator to look at; it builds no geometry, so its verify is 'look at the capture', never a geo stat.

steps.note: Auto-arrange the network so wires read top-to-bottom and nodes stop overlapping.

key_params.note: run after creating a batch of nodes

steps.note: Put the network editor in view and focus the pane on the relevant subtree.

key_params.note: frame the nodes you want to show

verify.cheap: (look - the right network is on screen)

steps.note: Screenshot the laid-out, framed graph. Now it is legible.

key_params.note: isolates the network editor for a clean grab

variants: frame_selected to zoom onto a specific node cluster before capture_ui.
node_organize / subnet_organize to group a busy network into a tidy subnet first.
Capturing the VIEWPORT (geometry) instead of the graph? Use snapshot, not capture_ui.
tips: layout_nodes is not optional - a stacked graph tells the operator nothing.
Frame before you capture; a captured graph zoomed to fit the whole huge network is as useless as a stacked one.
This is inspection, not construction - expect no geometry to change.

recipes.classify: match a camera to a reference photo - set intrinsics + background plate so a build registers to the picture
recipes.title: Camera match: add_camera (intrinsics + plate) -> aim -> snapshot-and-correct
recipes.summary: camera_match is a RECIPE, not a tool. Create a camera whose focal/aspect roughly match the photo, pin the photo as its background plate, aim it at the subject, then snapshot through it over the plate and correct until the built geometry's silhouette lines up. This is the camera step that image_to_3d_spine relies on.
recipes.governance: Single view gives silhouette + proportion match, NOT metric depth (for real depth use a scan / photogrammetry). Match add_camera resx/resy to the plate's pixel aspect or the overlay will not register. The plate is READ-CONFINED (working dir). You LOOK at the snapshot and correct focal/position - never auto-judge the match.

steps.note: Create the camera; set focal from EXIF if present (else estimate ~35mm), resx/resy to the plate size, and pin the photo as the background plate.

verify.cheap: (look through CONTROL_camera - plate shows as backdrop)

steps.note: Aim the camera at the subject or the ground/scale anchor so the framing matches the photo.
Render through CONTROL_camera over the plate. Compare silhouettes; nudge focal / camera position / subject scale until the built geometry sits where the real object sits. You judge this by eye.

verify.milestone_check: snapshot @CONTROL_camera (silhouettes line up with the reference)

variants: trace_raster the plate silhouette first to get a proportion guide to match the camera against.
Use this as the camera step inside image_to_3d_spine, then dispatch each element under its OUT_ null.
Ground the scale with a create_primitive grid sized to a known real dimension in the photo.
tips: resx/resy MUST match the plate aspect - a 16:9 plate under a 4:3 camera will never line up.
Focal is the biggest lever on perspective match; estimate, snapshot, correct.
One view = proportion, not depth. Do not expect a metrically correct model from a single photo.

recipes.classify: procedural texture / PBR material maps - author basecolor / roughness / normal / AO / height images
recipes.title: COP PBR maps: one master pattern -> derive normal+AO+color -> write the map set to disk
recipes.summary: The core image-texture workflow. Build ONE master mono pattern (fractal/worley/grunge noise) as a height layer, derive the normal and AO maps FROM it so they agree, tint a copy into a base color, then write the whole PBR set to disk (confined) ready to bind into a material. All procedural, all data-only - no code.
recipes.governance: COP layers are IMAGES, not SOP geometry - verify them by LOOKING (snapshot the COP view / open the written file), never read_geo_stats. Author ONE master height/pattern and DERIVE normal + AO from it so the maps agree (deriving each independently makes them fight). cop_rop_image output paths are READ-CONFINED (working dir). element_size on the noise is the master scale dial. Bind the finished maps via assign_usd_material's *_map slots.

steps.note: Author the master mono pattern - this doubles as the HEIGHT map and the source for normal/AO. element_size sets feature scale; octaves/roughness set detail.
Tint/grade a copy of the pattern into the BASE COLOR map (add worley/grunge variation first if you want material breakup). master_add/master_mult/master_gamma set the color.
Derive the tangent-space NORMAL map from OUT_height. scale sets bump strength; normal_type tangent.
Derive the ambient-occlusion map from OUT_height (crevices darken). view_radius/ray_count set quality.

verify.cheap: (look at OUT_ao - dark in the crevices)

steps.note: Write each map to disk (basecolor / normal / ao / height) as separate files in the working dir. One cop_rop_image per map. Paths are read-confined.

verify.cheap: confirm the written files exist in the working dir
verify.milestone_check: open the written maps (or snapshot a material using them)

variants: Metal/rust: swap cop_fractal_noise for cop_grunge_rust (or layer it) for corrosion breakup.
Cellular/stone/organic cells: cop_worley_noise as the master pattern instead of fractal.
Roughness map: cop_color_correct the pattern into a mono roughness layer (rough in the crevices).
Bind the set: assign_usd_material basecolor_map/normal_map/roughness_map/... = the written file paths.
Tileable: keep the noise tiled (worley `tiled`) or triplanar-project at shade time (cop_triplanar).
tips: Derive normal AND ao from the SAME height layer or they disagree and the surface looks wrong.
Layers are images - look at them; read_geo_stats does not read COP layers.
element_size is the single most important dial - set the real-world feature scale first, then add detail.

recipes.classify: bake texture maps FROM geometry - transfer hi-res detail (normal/AO/curvature/height) onto a low-res UV
recipes.title: COP bake: hi mesh + low UV mesh -> Bake Geometry Textures -> write the map set
recipes.summary: The 'bake my high-poly detail to maps' workflow. Bring a UV'd low-poly and a hi-detail high-poly into the copnet, run Bake Geometry Textures to project the high onto the low's UVs (normal/AO/curvature/height/etc.), then write each baked map to disk (confined). Feeds the same *_map slots as cop_pbr_material_maps.
recipes.governance: The LOW mesh MUST be UV'd first (uv it in SOPs) - the bake writes into UV space. Provide a hi-DETAIL high mesh and a clean low mesh; the bake_* toggles pick which maps to emit. tracing_mode + tangents govern normal-map correctness (wrong tangents = a normal map that lights inside-out). COP layers are images (look, don't read_geo_stats). cop_rop_image output is read-confined.

steps.note: Ensure the LOW mesh has clean UVs (bake target space). If it already has UVs, confirm them; else uv-map first.

key_params.note: UVs are the canvas the bake writes into

steps.note: Project the HIGH mesh's detail onto the LOW mesh's UVs. Toggle the maps you need (bake_normal/bake_occlusion/bake_curvature/bake_height). tangents/tracing_mode drive normal correctness.

verify.cheap: (look at OUT_baked - the projected detail in UV space)
verify.milestone_check: (look at the baked normal/AO in UV space - detail transferred, no gaps)

rop_opportunity.why: a ray-traced Karma texture bake (AO/curvature/normal from the hi mesh) is higher fidelity than the COP rasterize bake; running it is a gated render-bake EXECUTION.
rop_opportunity.propose_via: bake_karma_texture builds + wires the Karma texture-bake ROP onto the low UV mesh; the human fires the bake.
rop_opportunity.consent: the MCP BUILDS + WIRES the output ROP only; WRITING the file is the human's gated action - surface it as ready-to-fire via the gated_tool and explain what/where it writes, never .render()/.execute() it.

steps.note: Write each baked map to disk in the working dir (one cop_rop_image per map). Paths are read-confined.

variants: Curvature/cavity maps: enable bake_curvature/bake_cavity for edge-wear masks (drive roughness/dirt).
Position/thickness maps: bake_position / bake_thickness for SSS or effect masks.
Use cop_rasterize_setup first if you need to control the bake camera/space explicitly.
Bind the baked maps via assign_usd_material normal_map/... just like the procedural set.
tips: No UVs on the low mesh = nothing to bake into. UV first, always.
Wrong tangent basis makes the normal map light inside-out - match tangents to your renderer.
Baked maps are images in UV space - look at them; read_geo_stats does not apply.

recipes.classify: organic soft-merge / weld several shapes into one smooth blob (clay/metaball union boolean cannot do)
recipes.title: VDB organic merge: meshes -> SDF -> smooth union -> smooth -> back to poly
recipes.summary: The soft/organic counterpart to boolean. Convert the shapes to signed-distance VDBs, union them with a blend radius so they weld into one continuous surface (the 'melted clay' look), smooth, then convert back to polygons. Typed VDB CSG - no VEX, no code.
recipes.governance: voxelsize is the MASTER detail/cost dial - small voxels = huge memory, so probe mem before going fine. SDF union with a blend gives the smooth weld that boolean's hard seam cannot. RENORMALIZE the SDF (vdb_filter) after combining so it stays a valid distance field before meshing. Convert back to poly at the very end; a VDB is not a renderable mesh on its own.

steps.note: Convert each input shape to an SDF VDB. Same voxelsize for all so they combine cleanly. builddistance/SDF (not fog) is what you want for a union.
Union the SDFs. op=sdf, operation=union; use mixmethod/blend for a SMOOTH weld radius (the organic part). This is the CSG that boolean's hard edge cannot do.
Smooth + renormalize the merged SDF (op=smooth then a renormalize) so the field is valid and the surface is clean before meshing.

wrangle_opportunity.why: SDF-band shaping: read the VDB signed distance and remap only the near-surface band (custom fillet/erode profile) before meshing - a per-voxel SDF edit the fixed filter node cannot express.
wrangle_opportunity.consent: run via set_attrib_expr ONLY if the user has enabled allow_attrib_expr (explicit consent); otherwise propose the VEX text via vex_reference for the user to paste by hand, and EXPLAIN what it does and why (this is a teaching moment, not just an action).

steps.note: Convert the SDF back to polygons. adaptivity reduces polycount on flat areas; iso 0 for the SDF surface.

variants: Metaball / blobby-from-points: vdb_from_particles instead of vdb_from_polygons for a point cloud -> blob.
Native-volume lane: convert_volume (mode=isooffset) if you want a native Houdini volume instead of a VDB.
Hard mechanical union with a crisp seam: use boolean, not this - VDB union is for SOFT/organic welds.
Clean up after meshing: mesh_repair to close any tiny gaps and unify normals.
tips: Same voxelsize on every input SDF, or the union resamples and loses detail.
Renormalize after combine - an un-renormalized SDF meshes with artifacts.
Start coarse (large voxelsize), confirm the weld reads, then refine - fine voxels blow memory fast.

recipes.classify: export each piece / partition to its OWN file - per-name / per-group / per-attribute batch export
recipes.title: Batch export: partition the input -> one confined file per partition
recipes.summary: When you need one file PER piece (per fractured chunk, per instance type, per named part) instead of a single combined file. Make sure the input carries the partition key (a name/group/attribute), then batch_export writes one confined file per partition with a guard against a runaway split.
recipes.governance: batch_export splits by name | group | attribute and writes ONE file per partition into a CONFINED output_dir (defaults to the working dir). max_files is a runaway guard (default 512) - a split on a high-cardinality attribute can explode into thousands of files, so confirm the partition count first. For a single combined file, use export_geometry instead.

steps.note: Confirm the input carries the partition key and how many partitions it will make (distinct name/group/attribute values). This is the count max_files guards against.

key_params.note: check the split attribute exists + its cardinality

steps.note: Split and write one file per partition. split_by=name|group|attribute; output_dir confined; max_files caps the count. basename+format set the naming.

verify.cheap: confirm N files (== partition count) exist in output_dir
verify.milestone_check: list output_dir - one file per partition, count matches

rop_opportunity.why: the input is partitioned and each partition is ready to write; emitting one raw geometry file per partition is a gated batch WRITE.
rop_opportunity.propose_via: rop_geometryraw builds + wires the per-partition raw geometry ROP; the human fires the batch write.
rop_opportunity.consent: the MCP BUILDS + WIRES the output ROP only; WRITING the file is the human's gated action - surface it as ready-to-fire via the gated_tool and explain what/where it writes, never .render()/.execute() it.

variants: No partition key yet: assign_name (per piece) or group_create first, then split by that.
Fractured RBD: split_by=name after rbd_material_fracture (each Voronoi piece already carries a name).
One combined file instead: export_geometry (single ROP write).
Instance kit: split_by=attribute on a variant id to emit one file per instance type.
tips: Check partition cardinality BEFORE exporting - a split on @id can mean thousands of files; max_files stops it.
output_dir is confined to the working dir - an out-of-dir path is refused.
Name partitions meaningfully (assign_name) so the written filenames are usable.

recipes.title: Procedural tree / plant (SideFX Labs Tree Tools)
recipes.summary: Grow a procedural tree with the SideFX Labs tree suite: an OPTIONAL controller SOURCE (shared settings) -> trunk generator (base=controller) -> branch generators (one per level; the spine curve auto-wires down output 1) -> a leaf template + leaf generator. Base/pine/willow/umbrella are the same chain with different settings. Data-only; ramps stay at HDA default.

steps.note: OPTIONAL but recommended: a SOURCE node (0 inputs) holding tree-wide settings. Build it FIRST. seam_options=none while building (fast) -> boolean at the very end to weld branch seams; grav_strength for global droop(-)/lift(+). Skip it and the trunk still cooks bare.

the root: base=OUT_controller (input 0) so the tree inherits the controller. Builds trunk MESH (out0) + spine CURVE (out1). trunk_length/rad size it; enablebend+bend for lean; mesh_noise_amount=0 for a clean trunk.

LEVEL 1. input=OUT_trunk (mesh); the trunk's spine curve (output 1) AUTO-WIRES to input 1 - no curve param needed. mode=scatter + num_lat for count (or byedgelength). lat_angle/lat_length/radius shape it. Chain ANOTHER branch generator per level (input=previous OUT_branch), lowering lat_length/radius each level; del_prev resets the level tree.
OFF-CHAIN leaf template (one leaf/needle card). bend=0 => flat pine needle; width/dist/points shape it. Feeds the leaf generator's `leaf` input (input 2).

TERMINUS. input=final OUT_branch (mesh); the branch's spine curve (output 1) AUTO-WIRES to input 1; leaf=OUT_leaf (input 2). pack=1 to instance. num_lat lower => more leaves; enable_grav + grav_strength (-4..-5) droops foliage (willow).

variants: One-call instant tree: quick_basic_tree(input=<ground/pts>) replaces the whole chain (growgen<=8, EXPONENTIAL polycount).
Pine: simple_leaf bend=0 (flat needle), or use a small sub-branch as the leaf source; branches face up (angle_ramp_toggle off).
Willow: tree_leaf_generator enable_grav=1, grav_strength -4..-5 to droop the foliage.
A whole FOREST: build ONE tree (OUT_tree), then instance it via proc_biome_scatter / copy_to_points onto scattered points - never grow thousands of full trees.
Game LOD: maps_baker (WIRE-ONLY) bakes the tree onto a flat card -> diffuse/opacity/normal atlas; you fire the bake.
tips: tree_controller is a SOURCE (0 inputs) - build it FIRST and feed it into the trunk's `base`; it is optional (trunk cooks without it).
The spine CURVE rides OUTPUT 1 and auto-wires branch->branch->leaf on input 1 - you never pass a curve param.
seam_options=none while iterating (fast), boolean only at the end - the masterclass's core lever.
Repeat tree_branch_generator per level (2-4 typical), each input=the previous OUT_branch, lowering lat_length + radius each level.
Ramps (angle/length/radius falloff) stay at HDA default here; hand-author them on the node for a hero tree.
recipes.classify: procedural tree / plant generation (SideFX Labs tree tools) - controller source -> trunk -> branch levels (curve auto-wires) -> leaf template + leaf generator
recipes.governance: seam_options none while building (fast) -> boolean to finish; branch num_lat x levels and quick_basic_tree growgen are the polycount levers - watch mem. A forest = generate ONE tree then instance via proc_biome_scatter, never grow thousands of full Labs trees.

recipes.title: City block / downtown from a block plate
recipes.summary: Turn a footprint area into a believable city block: subdivide the block into lots, lay streets between settlement seeds, then mass and skin a building per lot. Roads and buildings merge into one street-level anchor. Feeds the city-street + Times-Square style demos.

steps.note: the downtown BLOCK plate - a flat 2D polygon that lot_subdivision recursively cuts. A grid (a few quads) is a clean generated block; swap in real OSM footprints for a real city (see variants).

key_params.rows/cols: 2-4 (a proper 2D block, not a single tri)
key_params.size: the block footprint in world units

steps.note: recursively subdivide the block into building LOTS (parcels). iterations is depth (clamped <=100); minlotsize stops it cutting past a usable parcel; irregularity breaks the grid-perfect look.

key_params.minlotsize: floor lot area so parcels stay buildable

steps.note: tag a per-lot id BEFORE any per-lot op (same discipline as proc_building). connect_type=prim, attrib_name=lot -> each parcel gets a stable class id for per-lot randomize / for_each.
street/intersection SEED points across the block - these become the settlement nodes the road graph connects. Keep the count low (a dozen or two); every seed becomes an intersection.
connect the seed points into a street GRAPH (polylines), filtering by angle/distance so you get plausible streets not a full mesh. Output polylines feed road_generator directly.

key_params.connectionlimit: cap connections per intersection for a cleaner grid

steps.note: build the road-surface mesh with intersections from the street-graph centerlines. width/modular_size set lane scale; resolution/subdivide drive polycount (this step multiplies prims fast - see governance).

key_params.resolution: keep low (10) unless you need smooth intersection fillets
key_params.subdivide: off for blockout, on only for hero

steps.note: per-lot height + facade variant (class=prim, name=height, dimensions=1 float). A normal distribution over height reads as a real skyline; a discrete variant id picks facade types downstream.

key_params.name: height
key_params.distribution: normal (skyline); add a second call: variant, uniformdiscrete for facade type

steps.note: extrude each lot up into a 3D blockout MASS (the input building_generator skins). Per-lot height via distance_attrib is the SAME known gap as proc_building - attribute-bound distance doesn't drive per-face cleanly; loop with for_each(piece,lot) + set_attrib_expr for true varied heights, or extrude uniform for a blockout.

key_params.distance: uniform mass height for a blockout
key_params.distance_attrib: height (per-lot; needs for_each metadata - see governance)

steps.note: slice the blockout masses into floors and skin them with facade modules -> the actual buildings. Cooks on the whole multi-mass block at once (no per-lot loop needed to skin). THIS IS THE HEAVY COOK: a single block skinned ~22k prims / ~89k pts - probe mem and gate before batching blocks.

key_params.sFacadePattern: grammar string for the facade rhythm

steps.note: combine the road mesh + the buildings into one street-level stream.
the deliverable anchor for the finished block - the stable handle demos / cameras / copy_to_points street-furniture read from.

variants: Real city: osm_import for real building footprints / road centerlines instead of the generated grid block (skip lot_subdivision, feed OSM footprints straight to the massing branch and OSM roads to road_generator).

Terrain-aware streets: insert pathfinding_global (input=street_graph, terrain=a terrain grid, REQUIRED) between settlement_connections and road_generator so roads follow least-cost paths over sloped ground - numberofpoints is EXPENSIVE (hard-capped 500k).
Street furniture: scatter along the roads + attribute_randomize + copy_to_points (pack=true) for lamps / signs / cars.
Hero facades: building_from_patterns with a tagged building_module library (pattern grammar strings) instead of building_generator's default modules.
tips: lot_subdivision wants a flat 2D polygon block - a grid or a closed create_curve+polyfill, not an open curve.
settlement_connections output IS polylines, so it feeds road_generator directly; pathfinding_global is only needed for terrain-aware routing.
Keep scatter seeds low - every seed becomes an intersection, and road_generator polycount scales with intersections x resolution.
Per-lot varied height is the known polyextrude attribute-bound-distance gap (see proc_building): loop with for_each(piece, lot) for true variation.
recipes.classify: whole city block / downtown / street grid (not one building) - subdivide a block into lots, street network between seeds, a building per lot
recipes.governance: building_generator is the memory blow-up: one skinned block is ~22k prims / ~89k pts - run mem before it and before batching multiple blocks; keep road_generator resolution low (10) and subdivide off for blockout. lot_subdivision iterations clamped <=100; pathfinding_global numberofpoints hard-capped (500k) and EXPENSIVE. copy_to_points street furniture MUST be pack=true. Per-lot height is the polyextrude attribute-bound-distance gap - for_each(piece) loop for true variation.

recipes.title: Weathering layers: edge wear, cavity dirt, contact rubble, top dust
recipes.summary: Layer age/dirt/wear onto a hard-surface prop: chip the hard edges, compute cavity (AO) and curvature masks, author a Cd wear tint from them, then drop ground-contact rubble and upward-facing dust. Outputs durable mask attributes (occlusion, convexity/concavity) for look-dev plus a visible Cd preview.

steps.note: recompute clean point normals FIRST - the occlusion and curvature masks are meaningless without correct N. If the prop has perfectly sharp CG edges, polybevel them first: sharp edges give no curvature gradient for the wear mask to grab.

key_params.mode: point (smooth) - the mask nodes read point N

steps.note: chip / erode the hard edges via a procedural VDB pass - breaks the CG-perfect silhouette so edges read as worn. Do this BEFORE the masks so occlusion/curvature are measured on the FINAL damaged surface. COST: voxel_res is a relative voxel size - smaller = finer = far more expensive; it also re-meshes (a beveled box goes ~26 -> ~15k prims), so any attribute computed before it is discarded.

key_params.voxel_res: 0.03-0.06 coarse for blockout; drop only for hero (VDB cost explodes)

steps.note: cavity / ambient-occlusion mask into point attr `occlusion` - the where-dirt-collects signal. Set colorout=off so you keep the MASK attribute and don't clobber Cd (the tint is authored later). Optionally wire an occluder mesh on input 1 for contact shadowing.

key_params.maxdist: cavity reach - larger catches broad recesses

steps.note: edge-wear masks: `convexity` (raised edges that rub bright/worn) and `concavity` (recesses that hold grime), into point attrs. viscolor=off so the Cd stays free for the tint step. These are the durable look-dev signals a shader ramps on.

key_params.method: 0-6 estimator; convexity/concavity mult+blur shape each side

steps.note: author a VISIBLE Cd wear tint from the convex/concave edges - the quick preview of the wear (bright worn edges, dark grimy recesses). This is the one step that WRITES Cd; do it before the dirt/snow accretion (they carry their own vertex colors).

key_params.convex_range_scale: how far the bright edge-wear reaches
key_params.concave_range_scale: how far the recess grime spreads

wrangle_opportunity.why: layered wear compositing: combine curvature (edge wear), occlusion (cavity dirt) and a height band into one f@wear mask with per-layer weights - a multi-input weathering blend the single-purpose color nodes cannot compose.
wrangle_opportunity.consent: run via set_attrib_expr ONLY if the user has enabled allow_attrib_expr (explicit consent); otherwise propose the VEX text via vex_reference for the user to paste by hand, and EXPLAIN what it does and why (this is a teaching moment, not just an action).

steps.note: ground-contact RUBBLE skirt where the prop meets the floor (the little debris pile at a wall/rock base). input 0 = the prop, input 1 = a ground surface (REQUIRED - a grid). finalcount caps the scattered debris; set keepobjectmesh=on so the prop survives into the merge.

key_params.ground: a grid the prop sits on (input 1, required)
key_params.finalcount: cap debris count (300 is plenty for a prop)
key_params.keepobjectmesh: on (keep the prop, not just the skirt)

steps.note: accumulate a shell on the UPWARD-facing faces - snow, dust, ash. angle is the max slope that holds accretion; snowheight is the depth and DEFAULTS TO 0 (no visible shell) so you MUST raise it. keeporiginal=on merges the shell with the prop.

key_params.angle: max face slope that holds accretion (default 60)

steps.note: the weathered deliverable anchor - carries the mask attrs (occlusion, convexity, concavity), the Cd preview, and the rubble+dust accretion for a shader / export to read.

variants: Fast curvature: fast_gaussian_curvature (single `curvature` attr, angle-defect) instead of measure_curvature when you just need one edge signal.
Height grime: color_gradient (Cd along Y) layered under edge_color for a top-clean / bottom-dirty vertical gradient.
Mask-driven damage: feed the occlusion/curvature attr as edge_damage `mask_attribute` so the chipping concentrates on exposed edges only.
No accretion: stop at OUT_cd for pure surface weathering (masks + tint) with no added rubble/dust geometry.
tips: Order matters: edge_damage RE-MESHES (VDB), so it must run before the mask nodes or their attributes are thrown away.
Keep colorout / viscolor OFF on the mask nodes - let exactly one step (edge_color / color_gradient) own Cd, or later tints fight each other.
occlusion + convexity + concavity are the payload for a shader ramp; Cd is just the viewport preview.
dirtskirt and snow_buildup ADD geometry (debris, shell) - they're scene-contact dressing; skip them for a clean texture-only pass.
recipes.classify: make a prop / hard-surface asset look aged / dirty / worn / weathered - cavity+edge masks driving a Cd tint, plus ground rubble and top dust
recipes.governance: edge_damage voxel_res is the cost lever - it re-meshes to VDB resolution (coarse 0.04 -> ~15k prims on a small prop; halving voxel_res roughly quadruples it). Probe mem before a fine pass or a batch of props. Mask nodes must run colorout/viscolor OFF so a single step owns Cd. dirtskirt needs a ground on input 1; snow_buildup snowheight defaults to 0 (invisible) and must be raised.

recipes.title: Climate-driven biome ecosystem (SideFX Labs Biome system)
recipes.summary: Cover a terrain with a believable, climate-driven plant ecosystem using the SideFX Labs Biome pipeline: define biomes + plant species (each with temperature/precipitation tolerances), bake the climate onto the terrain as heightfield layers, then scatter vegetation whose density follows those layers. A TIGHTLY-COUPLED config chain, not independent filters - the plant library rides scatter input 0 and the climate terrain rides scatter input 1.

steps.note: SOURCE. Define ONE biome's climate profile per node (biomename + tempaverage + precaverage) and chain several via `input` (input 0) so they merge into one biome library. Build this library FIRST; it seeds the climate the plants are judged against.

SOURCE = SCATTER INPUT 0. Define ONE plant species per node (plantname, type=tree|shrub, templower/temppref/tempupper, preclower/precpref/precupper, densitymax) and chain several via `input`. This plant library is what biome_scatter reads to place vegetation - it MUST wire to the scatter's input 0. Widen the tolerance band so at least one species is viable across the terrain's climate or the scatter emits 0 points.

Build the terrain (or start from import_heightfield / acquire_terrain on a real DEM). All biome heightfield ops run in NATIVE voxel space - build the terrain and its climate layers BEFORE any transform.

OPTIONAL (region-driven biomes). Wire the terrain to input 0; terraintype=heightfield, biomeinput=hf_layers to stay file-free. Outputs prepared Terrain (out0) + Biome Regions (out1). Skip it for a single-biome pass driven purely by the evolved climate.

The climate shaper: wire the terrain to input 0. Temperature drops with elevation (lapserate), precipitation is stripped on the lee of ridges (rain shadow: removebydir + rain_x/rain_z + anglespread), soil is culled on cliffs (removebyslope) and by noise (removebynoise). This is what makes the biome distribution read as physically plausible.

SCATTER INPUT 1. Wire the evolved terrain to input 0; bakes temperature / precipitation / soil / biome_color as named heightfield layers. usedefault=fill so cells with no biome still carry a climate. THIS output is the terrain the scatter reads on input 1.

key_params.usedefault: fill (constant climate for empty cells) vs transparent

steps.note: THE SCATTER (labs::biome_plant_scatter). WIRING IS LOAD-BEARING: the plant library (OUT_plants) rides input 0 and the climate terrain (OUT_climate) rides input 1; mode=Scatter on Input Terrain reads the baked layers to decide density/species. Emits one point per plant with meshpath/name/age attributes. densitymultiplier is the polycount lever - keep it LOW (0.05-0.2) or a 100x100 terrain explodes into millions of points (density 5 = ~5M).

Instance the plant assets onto the scattered points: source=plant/tree asset (input 0), target=OUT_ecosystem points (input 1). The scatter already wrote per-point pscale/orient/variant, so copies inherit natural size/lean/variation. pack=true ALWAYS (raw copy of thousands of trees = memory blowup).

key_params.id_attrib: match a variant/name attribute for multi-species asset selection

variants: Mask-driven (no biome definitions): proc_biome_scatter uses heightfield_maskbyfeature/occlusion/shadow -> heightfield_scatter instead of the climate library - reach for it when you want art-directed placement rather than physically-derived climate.

Self-contained preview: biome_scatter mode=Scatter on Test Terrain needs ONLY the plant library (input 0) - it builds its own test terrain and scatters onto it (no OUT_terrain/OUT_climate needed). Fast way to preview a plant library.

recipes.title: Procedural tiling / pattern synthesis (Wang tiles + Wave Function Collapse)
recipes.summary: Generate a controllable aperiodic tiling or algorithmic layout for procedural floors / walls / decoration / level layout. PRIMARY = SideFX Labs Wang tiles (self-contained, no attribute authoring): sample a stochastic aperiodic seed set, decode it to a rows x cols tiling, then instance a tile motif per cell. VARIANT = 2D Wave Function Collapse, which synthesises a layout that locally resembles a small sample (more control, but needs per-point tile-id `name` attributes).

steps.note: SOURCE. A fresh /obj geo of stochastic Wang-tile seeds - an aperiodic tiling seed set with NO periodic repeat. Self-contained (0 inputs). mode picks the sampling scheme; bVertexColor writes the tile code as color for the decoder to read.

key_params.bVertexColor: carry the tile code as vertex color

steps.note: Expands the seed set (input 0 = OUT_wang_seed) into the aperiodic tiling. mColorChannel selects which color channel carries the tile code (must match how the sample wrote it); mMode picks the decode scheme. The tiling is guaranteed edge-consistent and non-repeating - the whole point of Wang tiles for seamless floors/textures.

Instance a tile motif per cell: source = the tile asset (input 0), target = OUT_tiling points (input 1). This is where the abstract tiling becomes real decoration/floor/level geometry. Match a tile-code attribute with id_attrib for multi-tile sets (different tiles per code). pack=true ALWAYS.

key_params.id_attrib: match the decoded tile code to a piece attribute for multi-tile sets

variants: 2D Wave Function Collapse (locally-similar synthesis): wavefunction_collapse_2d input=<OUTPUT grid> sample=<SAMPLE grid>. BOTH inputs MUST carry a per-point string `name` attribute = the tile id (the SAMPLE's names supply the patterns; the OUTPUT's names are user constraints, empty string = unconstrained). Proven cook: 8x8 A/B checker sample -> 16x16 output = 256pts/225prims, errors=[]. Author the `name` grids interactively with wfc_initialize (blank rows x cols grid) + wfc_sample_paint (paint tile constraints - a GUI/viewport SOP; strokes cannot be issued headlessly), then solve. Use WFC when you need the output to resemble a specific authored sample; use Wang when you just need a fast, guaranteed-aperiodic tiling.
Pure layout (no instancing): stop at OUT_tiling and terminate with null as the scene anchor when you only need the tile-code point grid (e.g. to drive a downstream shader or export).
Texture tiling: the aperiodic tiling is ideal as a seamless, repeat-free base for cop_tile_pattern / trim-sheet UV layouts.
tips: Wang path is the reliable primary - both nodes are data-only and need NO attribute authoring, so it always cooks headlessly. WFC is more expressive but requires per-point `name` attributes on BOTH inputs, and the paint front-end (wfc_sample_paint) is interactive-only.
wang_tiles_decoder reads the tile code from the color channel the sample wrote (mColorChannel must match bVertexColor) - a channel mismatch decodes to a flat/garbage tiling.

WFC #1 failure mode is a missing point `name` attribute on an input (the HDA's internal reader raises), NOT wiring - author an empty-string `name` on the output grid and a distinct-token `name` on the sample.
iPatternSearchSize (WFC) is the cost knob (pattern neighbourhood, clamped <=8); iNumSolveAttempts retries a contradiction - raise it if the solve fails on a constrained sample.
recipes.classify: generate a controllable tiling / pattern / algorithmic layout (wang-tile texture, WFC tile synthesis) for procedural floors / walls / decoration / level layout
recipes.governance: copy_to_points MUST have pack=true (raw copy of a large tiling = memory blowup). Wang decoder mColorChannel must match the sample's bVertexColor channel. WFC needs a per-point string `name` on BOTH inputs or it errors; iPatternSearchSize is the cost knob (clamped <=8). wfc_sample_paint is interactive-only (GUI strokes) - not part of a headless chain.

recipes.title: Game-asset export: hi-res mesh -> retopo -> LODs -> UVs -> bake -> engine file
recipes.summary: Turn a finished hi-res mesh into a real-time game asset: decimate/retopo to a poly budget, build LODs, unwrap for lightmaps, then bake the hi->lo detail and export to an engine. The geometry steps cook; the bake and the engine export are WIRE-ONLY (built + wired + confined, fired by the operator).

steps.note: Decimate the hi-res mesh to a real-time poly budget (retopo pass). Use quad_remesh instead when you need clean animation-ready quad topology rather than a raw triangle decimation.

key_params.percentage: target as a % of input polys (e.g. 5-10 for a hero prop); or drive to an explicit target polycount
key_params.note: budget-aware -- this is the step that hits the polycount target, not the LOD step

steps.note: Build the LOD chain (LOD0..LODn) from the retopo'd base for engine distance-switching. gameres is the alternative when you want the full Labs game-res prep (naming/attribute cleanup) rather than just LOD generation.

key_params.lod_count: number of successive LODs to generate

rop_opportunity.why: distant LODs read best as camera-facing impostors; baking the impostor billboard atlas (multi-angle octahedral sheet) is a gated render-bake EXECUTION with no data-only substitute.
rop_opportunity.propose_via: bake_impostor_texture builds + wires the impostor camera-rig + bake for the far LOD; the human fires the bake.
rop_opportunity.consent: the MCP BUILDS + WIRES the output ROP only; WRITING the file is the human's gated action - surface it as ready-to-fire via the gated_tool and explain what/where it writes, never .render()/.execute() it.

steps.note: Auto-unwrap for lightmaps/textures -- the bake writes INTO this UV space, so it MUST run before the bake. Use uv for a hand-controlled projection/unwrap when autouv's islands are unacceptable.

key_params.use_existing_seams: false for a fresh auto unwrap; true to respect pre-marked seams
key_params.note: confirm a uv attribute lands before wiring the baker

steps.note: WIRE-ONLY. Project the hi-res detail onto the UV'd low mesh: in0 = low (@OUT_game_uv, the UV target), in1 = the hi-res mesh. Toggle normal/AO/curvature/height. Built + wired + output-confined; the OPERATOR fires the bake (do NOT execute). games_baker is the alternative for a game-engine-preset bake set.

key_params.tangents: match the target engine (wrong tangents = normal map lights inside-out)

verify.cheap: (confirm maps_baker built with in0=low UV mesh + in1=high mesh wired; do NOT render)

rop_opportunity.why: the game-asset map bake is wired WIRE-ONLY; the Karma-rendered normal/AO/ID bake to the engine texture set is a gated render-bake EXECUTION.
rop_opportunity.propose_via: bake_karma_texture builds + wires the Karma bake onto the retopo UV mesh; the human fires it.
rop_opportunity.consent: the MCP BUILDS + WIRES the output ROP only; WRITING the file is the human's gated action - surface it as ready-to-fire via the gated_tool and explain what/where it writes, never .render()/.execute() it.

steps.note: WIRE-ONLY export to a real-time engine. This is a Driver/ROP node: it references the geometry by a soppath (node_to_export = @OUT_game_uv), NOT by a wired SOP input, and writes to a confined export_path. Built + pointed; the OPERATOR fires the write (do NOT execute). Use vertex_animation_textures instead when the asset is a mesh-deformation/VAT export (soppath + confined map paths, same WIRE-ONLY discipline).

key_params.export_path: confined .fbx path in the working dir
key_params.note: ROP references geometry by path, not by wire -- confirm the soppath resolves to the final mesh

verify.cheap: (confirm the ROP built and node_to_export resolves to @OUT_game_uv; export_path is confined; do NOT render)

steps.note: Terminal anchor at the end of the SOP chain (@OUT_game_uv feeds it) so the graph has a stable scene-memory landmark for the exported asset.

variants: Quad workflow: quad_remesh instead of polyreduce for clean animation-ready quads.
Full game-res prep: gameres instead of lod_create (name/attribute cleanup + LODs).
Hand-authored UVs: uv instead of autouv when auto islands are unacceptable.
Engine-preset bake: games_baker instead of maps_baker for a game-engine map preset.
Vertex-animation export: vertex_animation_textures instead of rbd_to_fbx for VAT/mesh-deformation assets.
tips: polyreduce is where the poly BUDGET is hit -- lod_create only chains reductions off that base; check read_geo_stats against the target after retopo.
autouv MUST precede the bake -- no UVs = nothing to bake into.
maps_baker is a SOP with TWO inputs (in0 low / in1 high); rbd_to_fbx & vertex_animation_textures are Driver/ROP nodes referenced by soppath, not by a wired input -- a common wiring mistake.
Match the bake tangent basis to the target engine or the normal map lights inside-out.

Bake and export paths are read/write-confined to the working dir. autouv MUST run before the bake (bake writes into UV space). Match bake tangents to the target engine. Hit the poly budget at polyreduce/quad_remesh (LOD step only chains further reductions); verify polycount with read_geo_stats before the (operator-fired) export.

recipes.title: Bake maps: hi-res detail -> normal / AO / curvature on a lo-res UV mesh
recipes.summary: Transfer surface detail from a hi-res mesh onto texture maps (normal, AO, curvature, height) baked into a lo-res mesh's UVs. UV the low mesh first (the bake canvas), then WIRE the baker (in0=low, in1=high) and let the OPERATOR fire it into a confined dir. Optionally post-process the baked normal in COPs.

steps.note: The LOW mesh MUST have clean UVs -- the bake writes INTO UV space, so this is the canvas. If it already has UVs, confirm them; else unwrap here. Use uv for a hand-controlled projection when autouv's islands are unacceptable.

key_params.use_existing_seams: false for a fresh auto unwrap; true to respect pre-marked seams
key_params.note: no UVs on the low mesh = nothing to bake into

steps.note: WIRE-ONLY. The bake: in0 = low (@OUT_low_uv, UV target), in1 = the hi-detail mesh. Toggle bake_normal/bake_occlusion/bake_curvature/bake_height for the maps you need; output to a CONFINED dir. Built + wired + confined; the OPERATOR fires the bake render (do NOT execute). games_baker = game-engine map preset; simple_baker = the lightweight single-pass alternative.

key_params.tangents: match the target renderer (wrong tangents = normal map lights inside-out)

verify.cheap: (confirm maps_baker built with in0=low UV mesh + in1=high mesh wired, output confined; do NOT render)

rop_opportunity.why: maps_baker wires the bake network but rendered:False; a Karma-rendered bake of normal/AO/curvature is the gated render-bake EXECUTION.
rop_opportunity.propose_via: bake_karma_texture builds + wires the Karma bake over the hi/lo pair; the human fires the bake.
rop_opportunity.consent: the MCP BUILDS + WIRES the output ROP only; WRITING the file is the human's gated action - surface it as ready-to-fire via the gated_tool and explain what/where it writes, never .render()/.execute() it.

steps.note: OPTIONAL, WIRE-ONLY. Cop2 post-process of the baked normal (e.g. flip green channel for a DirectX/OpenGL target, or combine a detail normal). Built in a copnet; the OPERATOR composites/writes it. Use normal_combine to blend a baked base normal with a tiling detail normal. Skip entirely if the raw bake is final.

key_params.note: Cop2 image op -- look at the layer, do not read_geo_stats

verify.cheap: (confirm the Cop2 normal_map node built on the baked normal; do NOT composite)

variants: Game preset: games_baker instead of maps_baker for an engine-ready map set.
Lightweight: simple_baker for a fast single-pass normal/AO bake.
Hand UVs: uv instead of autouv when auto islands are unacceptable.
Detail normals: normal_combine to blend the baked normal with a tiling detail normal.
Curvature/cavity: enable bake_curvature for an edge-wear mask that drives roughness/dirt.
tips: UV the LOW mesh first, always -- the bake has no canvas otherwise.
maps_baker is a SOP with TWO inputs: in0 = low (UV'd), in1 = high (detail). Swapping them bakes nothing useful.
Match the tangent basis to your renderer or the normal map lights inside-out.
Baked maps are images in UV space -- inspect the layer, read_geo_stats does not apply to them.
normal_map/normal_combine are Cop2 image ops (post-process), not SOP geometry ops.

recipes.governance: WIRE-ONLY the bake: the recipe BUILDS + WIRES (in0=low UV mesh, in1=high detail) + confines the output dir; the OPERATOR fires the bake render -- never execute maps_baker/games_baker/simple_baker from the recipe. recompute joint orientations; set up_vector for straight chains (spine/fingers).

name joint groups (e.g. @name=arm* -> 'arm'). KineFX group syntax: a bare name is a group NAME, not a joint name.
